title.zh: 卷一百二十八 列傳第十六 劉基 宋濂 葉琛 章溢
title.en: Volume 128 Biographies 16: Liu Ji, Song Lian, Ye Chen, Zhang Yi
title.raw: 卷一百二十八 列傳第十六 劉基 宋濂 葉琛 章溢 Volume 128 Biographies 16: Liu Ji, Song Lian, Ye Chen, Zhang Yi

sentences.zh: 劉基，字伯溫，青田人。

translations.literal: Liu Ji, styled Bowen, was a native of Qingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, whose courtesy name was Bowen, came from Qingtian.

sentences.zh: 曾祖濠，仕宋為翰林掌書。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hao served the Song as Keeper of Documents in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Hao had served the Song dynasty as keeper of documents in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，邑子林融倡義旅。

translations.literal: When the Song perished, a townsman named Lin Rong raised a loyalist force.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Song, a fellow townsman named Lin Rong raised a loyalist militia.

sentences.zh: 事敗，元遣使簿錄其党，多連染。

translations.literal: The affair failed; the Yuan sent envoys to register his faction, and many were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising failed, the Yuan dispatched officials to register Lin's associates, and many innocent people were swept up in the dragnet.

sentences.zh: 使道宿濠家，濠醉使者而焚其廬，籍悉毀。

translations.literal: The envoy lodged at Hao's home on the road; Hao got the envoy drunk, burned his dwelling, and destroyed all the registers.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy happened to lodge at Hao's house along the way; Hao plied him with wine, then burned down the building and destroyed every register.

sentences.zh: 使者計無所出，乃為更其籍，連染者皆得免。

translations.literal: The envoy, at his wits' end, had the registers rewritten, and all who had been implicated were spared.
translations.idiomatic: With no other recourse, the envoy had new registers drawn up, and everyone who had been caught up in the case was spared.

sentences.zh: 基幼穎異，其師鄭復初謂其父爚曰：「君祖德厚，此子必大君之門矣。

translations.literal: Ji was precocious as a child; his teacher Zheng Fuchu said to his father Yao, "Your ancestors' virtue is deep—this boy will surely bring great honor to your house.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Ji showed unusual brilliance; his teacher Zheng Fuchu told his father Yao, "Your family has accumulated great merit over generations—this son is destined to bring your house great distinction.

sentences.zh: 」元至順間，舉進士，除高安丞，有廉直聲。

translations.literal: " In the Zhishun era of the Yuan he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Gao'an, and gained a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Yuan Zhishun period he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Gao'an, and earned a reputation for upright and incorruptible service.

sentences.zh: 行省辟之，謝去。

translations.literal: The provincial administration invited him to serve; he declined and left.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial administration recruited him, but he declined and withdrew from office.

sentences.zh: 起為江浙儒學副提舉，論御史失職，為台臣所阻，再投劾歸。

translations.literal: He was later raised to be associate educational intendant of Jiang-Zhe; he criticized censors for dereliction of duty, was blocked by the censorate, and again submitted a memorial of resignation and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed associate educational intendant for the Jiang-Zhe region; when he criticized the censors for neglecting their duties, the censorate blocked him, and he once more resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 基博通經史，於書無不窺，尤精象緯之學。

translations.literal: Ji was broadly versed in the classics and histories; there was no book he did not examine, and he was especially expert in astronomy and astrology.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had mastered the classics and histories; there was scarcely a book he had not read, and he was especially skilled in astronomy and astrological lore.

sentences.zh: 西蜀趙天澤論江左人物，首稱基，以為諸葛孔明儔也。

translations.literal: Zhao Tianze of western Shu, discussing figures of the lower Yangzi, ranked Ji first and considered him a match for Zhuge Kongming.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Tianze of western Shu assessed the leading men of the lower Yangzi region, he named Ji foremost and declared him the equal of Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 方國珍起海上，掠郡縣，有司不能制。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen rose on the sea, plundered prefectures and counties, and the officials could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen had risen from the sea routes, raiding prefectures and counties, and the local authorities could not bring him to heel.

sentences.zh: 行省復辟基為元帥府都事。

translations.literal: The provincial administration again recruited Ji as chief clerk of the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial administration again recruited Ji to serve as chief clerk in the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 基議築慶元諸城以逼賊，國珍氣沮。

translations.literal: Ji proposed building fortifications at the cities around Qingyuan to press the bandits; Fang Guozhen's spirit was dampened.
translations.idiomatic: Ji proposed fortifying the cities around Qingyuan to hem in the rebels, and Fang Guozhen's confidence faltered.

sentences.zh: 及左丞帖裏帖木兒招諭國珍，基言方氏兄弟首亂，不誅無以懲後。

translations.literal: When the left councillor Tie'ertiemuer came to negotiate with Fang Guozhen, Ji said the Fang brothers had led the rebellion and that without executing them there would be no warning for those who came after.
translations.idiomatic: When the left councillor Tie'ertiemuer was sent to negotiate with Fang Guozhen, Ji argued that the Fang brothers had instigated the rebellion and that unless they were punished, no lesson would be taught to future rebels.

sentences.zh: 國珍懼，厚賂基。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen was afraid and bribed Ji lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen grew fearful and offered Ji a lavish bribe.

sentences.zh: 基不受。

translations.literal: Ji did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ji refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 國珍乃使人浮海至京，賄用事者。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen then sent men by sea to the capital to bribe those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen then sent envoys by sea to the capital to bribe the men who held real power at court.

sentences.zh: 遂詔撫國珍，授以官，而責基擅威福，羈管紹興，方氏遂愈橫。

translations.literal: An edict then pacified Fang Guozhen and granted him office, while Ji was blamed for arrogating authority and was detained at Shaoxing; the Fang clan grew still more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict then granted Fang Guozhen amnesty and an official post, while Ji was accused of abusing his authority and was placed under detention at Shaoxing; the Fang clan grew bolder than ever.

sentences.zh: 亡何，山寇蜂起，行省復辟基剿捕，與行院判石抹宜孫守處州。

translations.literal: Before long mountain bandits swarmed forth; the provincial administration again recruited Ji to suppress them, and he defended Chuzhou together with the branch administration judge Shimo Yisun.
translations.idiomatic: Before long mountain bandits rose everywhere; the provincial administration recalled Ji to hunt them down, and he defended Chuzhou alongside the branch administration judge Shimo Yisun.

sentences.zh: 經略使李國鳳上其功，執政以方氏故抑之，授總管府判，不與兵事。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Li Guofeng reported his achievements, but the chief ministers, for the Fang clan's sake, suppressed them; he was given the post of judge of the chief commandery but was kept from military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commissioner Li Guofeng reported Ji's achievements to the court, but the chief ministers, mindful of the Fang clan, suppressed the report; Ji was appointed judge of the chief commandery but was denied any role in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 基遂棄官還青田，著《郁離子》以見志。

translations.literal: Ji then abandoned office and returned to Qingtian, writing the 《Yulizi》 to express his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Ji thereupon resigned and returned to Qingtian, where he wrote the 《Yulizi》 to set forth his convictions.

sentences.zh: 時避方氏者爭依基，基稍為部署，寇不敢犯。

translations.literal: At the time those fleeing the Fang clan vied to rely on Ji; he made some deployments, and the bandits did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: At that time everyone fleeing the Fang clan sought refuge with Ji; he organized a modest defense, and the raiders did not dare molest the area.

sentences.zh: 及太祖下金華，定括蒼，聞基及宋濂等名，以幣聘。

translations.literal: When Taizu took Jinhua and pacified Kuocang, he heard the names of Ji and Song Lian and sent gifts to invite them.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu captured Jinhua and secured Kuocang, he heard of Ji and Song Lian and sent envoys bearing gifts to invite them to his service.

sentences.zh: 基未應，總制孫炎再致書固邀之，基始出。

translations.literal: Ji did not respond; the chief controller Sun Yan wrote again firmly inviting him, and only then did Ji come forth.
translations.idiomatic: Ji did not respond at first; the chief controller Sun Yan wrote again with urgent invitations, and only then did Ji emerge from retirement.

sentences.zh: 既至，陳時務十八策。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he set forth eighteen policies on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his arrival he presented eighteen policy recommendations on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜，築禮賢館以處基等，寵禮甚至。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased, built the Hall for Honoring the Worthy to lodge Ji and the others, and favored them with the utmost courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and built the Hall for Honoring the Worthy to house Ji and his colleagues, treating them with the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以韓林兒稱宋後，遙奉之。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu, because Han Lin'er claimed descent from the Song, had acknowledged him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Han Lin'er claimed to be a scion of the Song, Taizu had acknowledged him as his nominal sovereign from afar.

sentences.zh: 歲首，中書省設御座行禮，基獨不拜，曰：「牧豎耳，奉之何為！

translations.literal: At the New Year the Secretariat set up the imperial seat and performed rites; Ji alone did not bow, saying, "He is but a shepherd boy—why serve him!
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year the Secretariat set up the imperial seat and performed the rites of obeisance; Ji alone refused to bow, saying, "He is nothing but a shepherd boy—why should we honor him!"

sentences.zh: 」因見太祖，陳天命所在。

translations.literal: " He then saw Taizu and explained where the Mandate of Heaven lay.
translations.idiomatic: " He then met with Taizu and explained where the Mandate of Heaven truly rested.

sentences.zh: 太祖問征取計，基曰：「士誠自守虜，不足慮。

translations.literal: Taizu asked about plans for conquest; Ji said, "Shicheng is a self-defending barbarian and is not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu asked for a strategy of conquest, Ji said, "Zhang Shicheng is merely holding his ground like a cornered beast and is not worth worrying about.

sentences.zh: 友諒劫主脅下，名號不正，地據上流，其心無日忘我，宜先圖之。

translations.literal: Youliang holds his lord hostage and coerces his subordinates; his title is not legitimate, his territory lies on the upper reaches, and his heart never forgets us for a day—we should deal with him first.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang holds his sovereign hostage and rules by coercion; his claim is illegitimate, his territory commands the upper Yangzi, and he thinks of destroying us every day—you should strike at him first.

sentences.zh: 陳氏滅，張氏勢孤，一舉可定。

translations.literal: When the Chen house is destroyed, the Zhang house will stand alone and can be settled in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Chen clan is destroyed, Zhang Shicheng will stand alone and can be brought down in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 然後北向中原，王業可成也。

translations.literal: Then turn north toward the Central Plains and the royal enterprise can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Then you can turn north toward the Central Plains, and the foundation of an empire can be laid.

sentences.zh: 」太祖大悅曰：「先生有至計，勿惜盡言。

translations.literal: " Taizu was greatly pleased and said, "Sir, you have a supreme plan—do not spare your words.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu was greatly pleased and said, "Sir, you have a master strategy—please speak without reserve.

sentences.zh: 」會陳友諒陷太平，謀東下，勢張甚，諸將或議降，或議奔據鐘山，基張目不言。

translations.literal: " Just then Chen Youliang took Taiping and planned to drive east; his momentum was very strong; some generals discussed surrender, others fleeing to hold Zhongshan; Ji opened his eyes wide and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " At that moment Chen Youliang had captured Taiping and was preparing to march east; his power was formidable, and some generals urged surrender while others proposed abandoning the capital for Zhongshan; Ji glared in silence and would not speak.

sentences.zh: 太祖召入內，基奮曰：「主降及奔者，可斬也。

translations.literal: Taizu summoned him within; Ji roused himself and said, "Those who advocate surrender or flight may be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu summoned him inside; Ji spoke with force: "Anyone who counsels surrender or flight deserves to be executed.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「先生計安出？

translations.literal: " Taizu said, "Sir, what plan do you propose?
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu asked, "Sir, what is your plan?

sentences.zh: 」基曰：「賊驕矣，待其深入，伏兵邀取之，易耳。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "The bandit is arrogant; wait until he advances deep, then ambush and intercept him—it is easy.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji replied, "The enemy has grown arrogant; wait until he advances deep into our territory, then cut him off with an ambush—it will be easy.

sentences.zh: 天道後舉者勝，取威制敵以成王業，在此舉矣。

translations.literal: By Heaven's way he who strikes later prevails; to take awe and control the enemy and accomplish the royal enterprise lies in this move.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favors those who strike second; to awe your foe, master the enemy, and lay the foundation of empire—all depends on this battle.

sentences.zh: 」太祖用其策，誘友諒至，大破之，以克敵賞賞基。

translations.literal: " Taizu used his plan, lured Youliang in, and routed him utterly; he rewarded Ji for defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu adopted his plan, lured Youliang into battle, and won a crushing victory; he offered Ji a reward for the triumph over the enemy.

sentences.zh: 基辭。

translations.literal: Ji declined.
translations.idiomatic: Ji declined the reward.

sentences.zh: 友諒兵復陷安慶，太祖欲自將討之，以問基。

translations.literal: Youliang's army again took Anqing; Taizu wished to lead the campaign in person and asked Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's forces recaptured Anqing; Taizu wished to lead the campaign personally and sought Ji's counsel.

sentences.zh: 基力贊，遂出師攻安慶。

translations.literal: Ji strongly approved, and he then marched out to attack Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Ji strongly urged him on, and Taizu marched out to attack Anqing.

sentences.zh: 自旦及暮不下，基請逕趨江州，搗友諒巢穴，遂悉軍西上。

translations.literal: From dawn to dusk it was not taken; Ji asked to press straight on to Jiangzhou and strike Youliang's nest, and he then led the whole army west.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until evening the city still held; Ji proposed marching directly on Jiangzhou to strike at Youliang's base, and Taizu led the entire army westward.

sentences.zh: 友諒出不意，帥妻子奔武昌，江州降。

translations.literal: Youliang, caught unawares, led his wife and children in flight to Wuchang; Jiangzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard, Youliang fled with his family to Wuchang, and Jiangzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其龍興守將胡美遣子通款，請勿散其部曲。

translations.literal: Hu Mei, the defending general at Longxing, sent his son to offer submission and asked that his troops not be dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mei, the defending general at Longxing, sent his son to negotiate surrender and pleaded that his troops not be broken up.

sentences.zh: 太祖有難色。

translations.literal: Taizu looked troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu hesitated.

sentences.zh: 基從後蹋胡床。

translations.literal: Ji kicked the folding chair from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Ji kicked the back of Taizu's folding chair.

sentences.zh: 太祖悟，許之。

translations.literal: Taizu understood and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu understood the signal and agreed.

sentences.zh: 美降，江西諸郡皆下。

translations.literal: Mei surrendered, and all the prefectures of Jiangxi submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mei surrendered, and all the prefectures of Jiangxi fell.

sentences.zh: 基喪母，值兵事未敢言，至是請還葬。

translations.literal: Ji had lost his mother; because of military affairs he had not dared speak of it; now he asked to return and bury her.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's mother had died, but with war raging he had not dared request leave; now he asked permission to return home for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 會苗軍反，殺金、處守將胡大海、耿再成等，浙東搖動。

translations.literal: Just then the Miao army rebelled, killing the defending generals of Jin and Chu, Hu Dahai and Geng Zaicheng, and eastern Zhejiang was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Miao army rebelled, killing the defending generals Hu Dahai and Geng Zaicheng at Jin and Chu, and all of eastern Zhejiang was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 基至衢，為守將夏毅諭安諸屬邑，復與平章邵榮等謀復處州，亂遂定。

translations.literal: Ji reached Qu, instructed the defending general Xia Yi to pacify the subordinate counties, and again with the pingzhang Shao Rong and others planned to recover Chuzhou; the disorder was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ji reached Quzhou, helped the defending general Xia Yi pacify the surrounding counties, and together with the pingzhang Shao Rong and others planned the recovery of Chuzhou; the rebellion was soon suppressed.

sentences.zh: 國珍素畏基，致書唁。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen had always feared Ji and sent a letter of condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen had long feared Ji and sent a letter of condolence for his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 基答書，宣示太祖威德，國珍遂入貢。

translations.literal: Ji replied, proclaiming Taizu's might and virtue, and Fang Guozhen then sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote back, expounding Taizu's power and benevolence, and Fang Guozhen thereupon submitted tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖數以書即家訪軍國事，基條答悉中機宜。

translations.literal: Taizu repeatedly sent letters to his home to consult on military and state affairs; Ji's itemized replies all hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu repeatedly wrote to him at home to consult on military and state affairs, and Ji's detailed replies invariably proved exactly right.

sentences.zh: 尋赴京，太祖方親援安豐。

translations.literal: Soon he went to the capital; Taizu was personally relieving Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to the capital, where Taizu was personally leading a relief force to Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 基曰：「漢、吳伺隙，未可動也。

translations.literal: Ji said, "Han and Wu are watching for an opening—you must not move yet.
translations.idiomatic: Ji warned, "Chen Youliang and Zhang Shicheng are watching for an opening—you must not move yet.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 友諒聞之，乘間圍洪都。

translations.literal: Youliang heard of it and seized the interval to besiege Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang heard of the expedition and seized the opportunity to besiege Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「不聽君言，幾失計。

translations.literal: Taizu said, "Had I not listened to your words, I would nearly have lost my plan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Had I listened to you, I would not have come so close to disaster.

sentences.zh: 」遂自將救洪都，與友諒大戰鄱陽蝴，一日數十接。

translations.literal: " He then personally led the relief of Hongdu and fought a great battle with Youliang at Poyang Lake; in one day there were several dozen engagements.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led the relief of Hongdu in person and fought a great battle with Youliang on Poyang Lake, with dozens of clashes in a single day.

sentences.zh: 太祖坐胡床督戰，基侍側，忽躍起大呼，趣太祖更舟。

translations.literal: Taizu sat on a folding chair directing the battle; Ji attended at his side, then suddenly leaped up and shouted, urging Taizu to change boats.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sat on a folding chair directing the battle while Ji stood at his side; suddenly Ji leaped up and shouted, urging Taizu to change boats at once.

sentences.zh: 太祖倉卒徙別舸，坐未定，飛礮擊舊所御舟立碎。

translations.literal: Taizu hastily moved to another vessel; before he was seated, a flying projectile struck the boat he had just left and shattered it instantly.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu scrambled onto another vessel; before he had even taken his seat, a cannonball struck the boat he had just left and shattered it to splinters.

sentences.zh: 友諒乘高見之，大喜。

translations.literal: Youliang, looking down from on high, saw it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang, watching from higher ground, saw the explosion and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 而太祖舟更進，漢軍皆失色。

translations.literal: But Taizu's boat advanced again, and the Han army all lost color.
translations.idiomatic: But Taizu's new boat pressed forward, and Youliang's entire army turned pale with dismay.

sentences.zh: 時湖中相持，三日未決，基請移軍湖口扼之，以金木相犯日決勝，友諒走死。

translations.literal: At the time the two sides faced each other on the lake; after three days there was no decision; Ji asked to move the army to Hukou to block them; on the day when metal and wood clash, victory was decided; Youliang fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: The two fleets had faced each other on the lake for three days without a decision; Ji proposed shifting the army to Hukou to block the enemy's escape, and on the day when the elemental signs favored metal over wood, the battle was decided—Youliang fled and was killed.

sentences.zh: 其後太祖取士誠，北伐中原，遂成帝業，略如基謀。

translations.literal: Afterward Taizu took Shicheng, marched north against the Central Plains, and thus achieved the imperial enterprise, largely as Ji had planned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Taizu defeated Zhang Shicheng, marched north into the Central Plains, and founded the dynasty—largely along the lines Ji had laid out.

sentences.zh: 吳元年以基為太史令，上《戊申大統曆》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu, Ji was made Director of the Imperial Observatory and presented the 《Wushen Grand Unity Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu regime, Ji was appointed Director of the Imperial Observatory and presented the 《Wushen Grand Unity Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 熒惑守心，請下詔罪己。

translations.literal: When Mars stayed in the Heart constellation, he asked that an edict of self-blame be issued.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars lingered in the Heart constellation, he urged the court to issue an edict of self-reproach.

sentences.zh: 大旱，請決滯獄。

translations.literal: During a great drought he asked that stagnant cases in prison be decided.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought he urged that long-pending cases in prison be resolved.

sentences.zh: 即命基平反，雨隨注。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered to review and redress cases; rain poured down at once.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu immediately ordered Ji to review and redress wrongful convictions, and rain fell in torrents.

sentences.zh: 因請立法定制，以止濫殺。

translations.literal: He then asked to establish laws and fix institutions to stop indiscriminate killing.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged the establishment of laws and institutions to curb arbitrary executions.

sentences.zh: 太祖方欲刑人，基請其故，太祖語之以夢。

translations.literal: Taizu was about to punish someone; Ji asked the reason, and Taizu told him of a dream.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was about to execute someone, Ji asked the reason; Taizu told him of a dream he had had.

sentences.zh: 基曰：「此得土得眾之象，宜停刑以待。

translations.literal: Ji said, "This is an omen of gaining territory and winning the people; you should halt executions and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "This dream foretells that you will gain territory and win the people's loyalty; you should suspend executions and wait.

sentences.zh: 」後三日，海寧降。

translations.literal: " Three days later Haining surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days later Haining surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，悉以囚付基縱之。

translations.literal: Taizu was pleased and handed all the prisoners to Ji to release.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and handed all the prisoners over to Ji to set free.

sentences.zh: 尋拜御史中丞兼太史令。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Director of the Imperial Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Censor-in-Chief while retaining his post as Director of the Imperial Observatory.

sentences.zh: 太祖即皇帝位，基奏立軍衛法，初定處州稅糧，視宋制畝加五合，惟青田命毋加，曰：「令伯溫鄉里世世為美談也。

translations.literal: When Taizu assumed the imperial throne, Ji memorialized to establish military guard laws and first fixed the grain tax of Chuzhou at five he more per mu than the Song system; only Qingtian was ordered not to increase it, with the words, "Let Bowen's home district be praised for generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Ji memorialized to establish military guard regulations and set Chuzhou's grain tax five he higher per mu than under the Song system; only Qingtian was exempted, with the remark, "Let Bowen's homeland be a subject of praise for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 」帝幸汴梁，基與左丞相善長居守。

translations.literal: " The emperor visited Bianliang; Ji and the left chief councillor Shanchang remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor traveled to Bianliang, Ji and the left chief councillor Li Shanchang remained behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 基謂宋、元寬縱失天下，今宜肅紀綱。

translations.literal: Ji said the Song and Yuan had lost the realm through leniency and indulgence; now discipline should be tightened.
translations.idiomatic: Ji argued that the Song and Yuan had lost the empire through laxity and indulgence, and that the new dynasty must enforce strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 令御史糾劾無所避，宿衛宦侍有過者，皆啟皇太子置之法，人憚其嚴。

translations.literal: He ordered censors to impeach without avoidance; palace guards and eunuch attendants who erred were all reported to the crown prince for punishment; people feared his severity.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the censors to impeach without fear or favor; any palace guard or eunuch attendant who transgressed was reported to the crown prince for punishment, and everyone feared his severity.

sentences.zh: 中書省都事李彬坐貪縱抵罪，善長素匿之，請緩其獄。

translations.literal: Li Bin, a chief clerk of the Secretariat, was guilty of corruption and indulgence and was sentenced; Shanchang had long concealed him and asked to delay his case.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bin, a chief clerk of the Secretariat, was convicted of corruption and sentenced to death; Li Shanchang, who had long shielded him, pleaded for a delay in carrying out the sentence.

sentences.zh: 基不聽，馳奏。

translations.literal: Ji would not listen and sent a rapid memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Ji refused and sent an urgent memorial to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's reply granted approval.

sentences.zh: 方祈雨，即斬之。

translations.literal: Just as rain was being prayed for, he was beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was praying for rain, Ji had him executed immediately.

sentences.zh: 由是與善長忤。

translations.literal: From this he came into conflict with Shanchang.
translations.idiomatic: From this point he fell out with Li Shanchang.

sentences.zh: 帝歸，愬基僇人壇壝下，不敬。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he complained that Ji had executed a man below the altar terrace, which was disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he accused Ji of having executed a man below the altar terrace, an act of disrespect.

sentences.zh: 諸怨基者亦交譖之。

translations.literal: Those who resented Ji also joined in slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bore grudges against Ji joined in denouncing him.

sentences.zh: 會以旱求言，基奏：「士卒物故者，其妻悉處別營，凡數萬人，陰氣鬱結。

translations.literal: Just then, because of drought, the court sought advice; Ji memorialized, "The wives of soldiers who have died are all kept in separate camps, numbering tens of thousands; yin energy is pent up.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought advice because of the drought, Ji memorialized: "The widows of soldiers who died in service are all confined to separate camps—tens of thousands of women whose grief has no outlet; yin energy is pent up throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 工匠死，胔骸暴露，吳將吏降者皆編軍戶，足幹和氣。

translations.literal: When artisans die their corpses lie exposed; Wu generals and officials who surrendered are all enrolled as military households—enough to disturb harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans who die are left unburied; surrendered Wu generals and officials are all enrolled as military households—these practices are enough to disrupt the harmony of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，旬日仍不雨，帝怒。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words, but after ten days still there was no rain, and the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice, but after ten days still no rain fell, and the emperor grew angry.

sentences.zh: 會基有妻喪，遂請告歸。

translations.literal: Just then Ji had a wife's death and asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Ji happened to be mourning his wife and requested leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 時帝方營中都，又銳意滅擴廓。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was building the central capital and was also intent on destroying Kökö Temür.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was building a central capital and was also determined to destroy Kökö Temür.

sentences.zh: 基瀕行，奏曰：「鳳陽雖帝鄉，非建都地。

translations.literal: As Ji was about to depart, he memorialized, "Fengyang, though the emperor's homeland, is not a place to establish the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Ji was about to leave, he memorialized: "Fengyang, though it is your native district, is not a suitable site for the capital.

sentences.zh: 王保保未可輕也。

translations.literal: Wang Baobao must not be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Baobao must not be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 」已而定西失利，擴廓竟走沙漠，迄為邊患。

translations.literal: " Soon after, the Dingxi campaign failed; Kökö Temür ultimately fled to the desert and remained a frontier menace to the end.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the campaign in Dingxi failed; Kökö Temür fled into the desert and remained a border threat for years to come.

sentences.zh: 其冬，帝手詔敘基勳伐，召赴京，賜賚甚厚，追贈基祖、父皆永嘉郡公。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor personally drafted an edict recounting Ji's achievements, summoned him to the capital, bestowed gifts very generously, and posthumously enfeoffed Ji's grandfather and father both as Dukes of Yongjia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor issued a personal edict recounting Ji's achievements, summoned him back to the capital, lavished rich gifts upon him, and posthumously enfeoffed both Ji's grandfather and father as Dukes of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 累欲進基爵，基固辭不受。

translations.literal: Repeatedly they wished to advance Ji's rank; Ji firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly offered to advance Ji's rank, but Ji steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以事責丞相李善長，基言：「善長勳舊，能調和諸將。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu blamed Chief Councillor Li Shanchang over an affair; Ji said, "Shanchang is an old merit-holder and can harmonize the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Taizu blamed Chief Councillor Li Shanchang over a matter, Ji said, "Shanchang is a veteran of the founding campaigns and knows how to keep the generals in harmony.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「是數欲害君，君乃為之地耶？

translations.literal: " Taizu said, "He has several times wished to harm you—yet you plead his case?
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu said, "He has tried to harm you more than once—yet you plead on his behalf?

sentences.zh: 吾行相君矣。

translations.literal: I am about to make you chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: I am about to make you chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 」基頓首曰：「是如易柱，須得大木。

translations.literal: " Ji bowed his head and said, "That would be like replacing a pillar—you need a great timber.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji kowtowed and replied, "That would be like replacing a pillar—you need a massive timber.

sentences.zh: 若束小木為之，且立覆。

translations.literal: If you bind small timbers to make it, it will soon topple.
translations.idiomatic: If you lash together only small timbers, the structure will soon collapse.

sentences.zh: 」及善長罷，帝欲相楊憲。

translations.literal: " When Shanchang was dismissed, the emperor wished to make Yang Xian chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shanchang was removed, the emperor wished to appoint Yang Xian as chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 憲素善基，基力言不可，曰：「憲有相才無相器。

translations.literal: Xian had always been on good terms with Ji; Ji spoke forcefully that it would not do, saying, "Xian has the talent of a councillor but not the capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had long been friendly with Ji, but Ji strongly objected, saying, "Xian has the talent of a minister but not the temperament for the post.

sentences.zh: 夫宰相者，持心如水，以義理為權衡，而己無與者也，憲則不然。

translations.literal: A chief councillor holds his heart like water, takes righteousness and principle as his balance, and does not insert himself—Xian is not so.
translations.idiomatic: A true chief councillor keeps his heart level as water, weighs all matters by righteousness and principle, and does not push his own interests—Xian is not such a man.

sentences.zh: 」帝問汪廣洋，曰：「此褊淺殆甚於憲。

translations.literal: " The emperor asked about Wang Guangyang; he said, "This one is narrow and shallow—he is probably even worse than Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked about Wang Guangyang; Ji said, "He is narrow-minded and shallow—likely even worse than Xian.

sentences.zh: 」又問胡惟庸，曰：「譬之駕，懼其僨轅也。

translations.literal: " He then asked about Hu Weiyong; Ji said, "It is like driving a carriage—I fear he will overturn the shafts.
translations.idiomatic: " Asked about Hu Weiyong, Ji said, "It is like putting him in charge of the chariot—I fear he would overturn the shafts.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾之相，誠無逾先生。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "For my chief councillor there is truly none who surpasses you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "For chief councillor there is truly no one who surpasses you, sir.

sentences.zh: 」基曰：「臣疾惡太甚，又不耐繁劇，為之且孤上恩。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "Your servant hates evil too fiercely and cannot bear complicated affairs; to do it would only estrange your grace.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji replied, "I hate wickedness too fiercely and cannot bear the weight of such duties; if I took the post I would only disappoint your trust.

sentences.zh: 天下何患無才，惟明主悉心求之，目前諸人誠未見其可也。

translations.literal: Under Heaven why worry that there is no talent? Only let an enlightened ruler seek it with all his heart—the men before us truly do not seem fit.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is not lacking in talent; an enlightened ruler need only seek it wholeheartedly—but none of those now before us seem truly fit for the role.

sentences.zh: 」後憲、廣洋、惟庸皆敗。

translations.literal: " Later Xian, Guangyang, and Weiyong all came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: " In time Yang Xian, Wang Guangyang, and Hu Weiyong all met with ruin.

sentences.zh: 三年授弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made academician of the Hall for Promoting Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the reign he was appointed academician of the Hall for Promoting Literature.

sentences.zh: 十一月大封功臣，授基開國翊運守正文臣、資善大夫、上護軍，封誠意伯，祿二百四十石。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the meritorious were greatly enfeoffed; Ji was given the titles Founding Assistant in Upholding the Mandate, Upright Civil Minister, Grand Master of Fostering Goodness, and Senior Guardian of the Army, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengyi with a stipend of two hundred forty piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the founding meritorious officials were enfeoffed on a grand scale; Ji received the titles Founding Assistant in Upholding the Mandate, Upright Civil Minister, Grand Master of Fostering Goodness, and Senior Guardian of the Army, and was created Marquis of Chengyi with a stipend of two hundred forty piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 明年賜歸老於鄉。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted to return home in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was permitted to retire to his native district.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗手書問天象。

translations.literal: The emperor once wrote in his own hand to ask about celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wrote in his own hand to inquire about celestial omens.

sentences.zh: 基條答甚悉而焚其草。

translations.literal: Ji answered item by item very fully and burned the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied in detailed points and then burned the draft.

sentences.zh: 大要言霜雪之後，必有陽春，今國威已立，宜少濟以寬大。

translations.literal: In general he said that after frost and snow there must be spring; now the nation's majesty is established and it should be somewhat tempered with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In essence he wrote that after frost and snow spring must come; now that the empire's authority was secure, policy should be tempered with greater leniency.

sentences.zh: 基佐定天下，料事如神。

translations.literal: Ji assisted in settling the realm; his foresight of affairs was like a god's.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had helped establish the dynasty, and his foresight in affairs seemed almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 性剛嫉惡，與物多忤。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and hated evil; he clashed with many people.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and intolerant of evil, and he clashed with many around him.

sentences.zh: 至是還隱山中，惟飲酒弈棋，口不言功。

translations.literal: By then he returned to seclusion in the mountains, only drinking wine and playing chess, never speaking of his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had withdrawn to the mountains, drinking wine and playing chess, never speaking of his achievements.

sentences.zh: 邑令求見不得，微服為野人謁基。

translations.literal: The district magistrate sought to see him but could not; he put on plain clothes as a rustic and visited Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The district magistrate could not obtain an audience; he disguised himself as a commoner and went to visit Ji.

sentences.zh: 基方濯足，令從子引入茆舍，炊黍飯令。

translations.literal: Ji was just washing his feet; the magistrate had his nephew lead him into a thatched hut and cooked millet for the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was washing his feet; the magistrate had his nephew lead the visitor into a thatched hut and served him a meal of millet.

sentences.zh: 令告曰：「某青田知縣也。

translations.literal: The magistrate announced, "I am the magistrate of Qingtian.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate then revealed, "I am the magistrate of Qingtian.

sentences.zh: 」基驚起稱民，謝去，終不復見。

translations.literal: " Ji started up in surprise, addressed him as a commoner, apologized and left, and never saw him again.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji rose in alarm, addressed him as a commoner rather than an official, apologized, and departed—never granting him another meeting.

sentences.zh: 其韜跡如此，然究為惟庸所中。

translations.literal: His concealment of himself was thus, yet in the end he was struck down by Weiyong.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his manner of hiding from the world—yet in the end he was destroyed by Hu Weiyong.

sentences.zh: 初，基言甌、括間有隙地曰談洋，南抵閩界，為鹽盜藪，方氏所由乳，請設巡檢司守之。

translations.literal: Earlier Ji said that between Ou and Kuo there was open land called Tanyang, reaching south to the Fujian border, a lair of salt smugglers where the Fang clan had been nurtured; he asked to establish an inspection office to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ji had reported that between Ou and Kuo lay a tract of open land called Tanyang, reaching south to the Fujian border—a haunt of salt smugglers and a stronghold nurtured by the Fang clan—and he had requested that an inspection office be established to guard it.

sentences.zh: 奸民弗便也。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt local interests found this inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 會茗洋逃軍反，吏匿不以聞。

translations.literal: Just then deserters at Mingyang rebelled; officials concealed it and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: When deserters at Mingyang rebelled, local officials concealed the news and failed to report it.

sentences.zh: 基令長子璉奏其事，不先白中書省。

translations.literal: Ji had his eldest son Lian memorialize the affair without first informing the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had his eldest son Lian memorialize the matter directly, without first notifying the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 胡惟庸方以左丞掌省事，挾前憾，使吏訐基，謂談洋地有王氣，基圖為墓，民弗與，則請立巡檢逐民。

translations.literal: Hu Weiyong was then left vice-councillor managing Secretariat affairs; bearing an old grudge, he had officials impeach Ji, saying Tanyang land had royal qi, Ji plotted a tomb there, the people would not yield, and so he asked to establish an inspection office to drive the people away.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Weiyong, then serving as left vice-councillor in charge of Secretariat affairs, seized on an old grudge and had officials accuse Ji of claiming that Tanyang possessed royal qi, of plotting to build his tomb there, and of establishing an inspection office to drive out the people when they resisted.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不罪基，然頗為所動，遂奪基祿。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish Ji, yet was somewhat moved by it, and thus stripped Ji of his stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not convict Ji, but was somewhat swayed by the accusations and stripped him of his stipend.

sentences.zh: 基懼入謝，乃留京，不敢歸。

translations.literal: Ji feared to enter and apologize, and so remained in the capital, not daring to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Ji feared to go to court and apologize, and so remained in the capital, not daring to return home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，惟庸相，基大慼曰：「使吾言不驗，蒼生福也。

translations.literal: Before long Weiyong became chief councillor; Ji grieved greatly and said, "If my words are not borne out, it will be the people's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hu Weiyong became chief councillor; Ji grieved deeply and said, "If my words prove wrong, it will be a blessing for the people.

sentences.zh: 」憂憤疾作。

translations.literal: " Grief and anger brought on illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Grief and indignation brought on his illness.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，帝親制文賜之，遣使護歸。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year the emperor personally composed a text and bestowed it, sending envoys to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year the emperor composed a personal message of grace and sent envoys to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 抵家，疾篤，以《天文書》授子璉曰：「亟上之，毋令後人習也。

translations.literal: Upon reaching home his illness was grave; he gave his son Lian the Astronomical Treatise and said, "Quickly present it to the throne—do not let later generations study it.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached home his illness was grave; he handed his son Lian the Astronomical Treatise and said, "Present this to the throne at once—do not let later generations study it.

sentences.zh: 」又謂次子璟曰：「夫為政，寬猛如迴圈。

translations.literal: " He also told his second son Jing, "In governing, leniency and severity are like a turning wheel.
translations.idiomatic: " He also told his second son Jing, "In governing, leniency and severity revolve like a wheel.

sentences.zh: 當今之務在修德省刑，祈天永命。

translations.literal: The task of the present is to cultivate virtue and reduce punishments, praying Heaven for enduring mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The urgent task now is to cultivate virtue and reduce punishments, praying Heaven for a mandate that endures.

sentences.zh: 諸形勝要害之地，宜與京師聲勢連絡。

translations.literal: All strategic and vital places should be linked in power with the capital.
translations.idiomatic: All strategic strongpoints should be linked in strength with the capital.

sentences.zh: 我欲為遺表，惟庸在，無益也。

translations.literal: I wished to make a death memorial, but with Weiyong in power it would be useless.
translations.idiomatic: I had wished to leave a final memorial, but with Weiyong in power it would serve no purpose.

sentences.zh: 惟庸敗後，上必思我，有所問，以是密奏之。

translations.literal: After Weiyong's fall the emperor will surely think of me; if he asks anything, secretly memorialize this.
translations.idiomatic: After Weiyong falls, the emperor will surely think of me; if he inquires, submit this in a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 」居一月而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: " After one month he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: " A month later he died, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 基在京病時，惟庸以醫來，飲其藥，有物積腹中如拳石。

translations.literal: When Ji was ill in the capital, Weiyong sent a physician; he drank the medicine and a mass accumulated in his belly like a fist-sized stone.
translations.idiomatic: While Ji lay ill in the capital, Weiyong sent a physician; after taking the medicine, a hard mass formed in his belly the size of a fist.

sentences.zh: 其後中丞塗節首惟庸逆謀，並謂其毒基致死雲。

translations.literal: Later Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Jie exposed Weiyong's treasonous plot and also said he had poisoned Ji to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Jie exposed Hu Weiyong's treasonous plot and alleged that he had poisoned Ji to death.

sentences.zh: 基虯髯，貌修偉，慷慨有大節，論天下安危，義形於色。

translations.literal: Ji had curling beard, a tall and imposing appearance, was magnanimous with great integrity, and when discussing the realm's safety or peril, righteousness showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wore a curling beard and had a tall, imposing bearing; he was magnanimous and possessed of great integrity, and when he spoke of the empire's safety or peril, righteousness showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 帝察其至誠，任以心膂。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived his utmost sincerity and entrusted him as his innermost support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor perceived his utter sincerity and entrusted him as his closest confidant.

sentences.zh: 每召基，輒屏人密語移時。

translations.literal: Whenever he summoned Ji, he would dismiss attendants and speak in secret for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he summoned Ji, he dismissed everyone else and spoke with him in private for long stretches.

sentences.zh: 基亦自謂不世遇，知無不言。

translations.literal: Ji also considered himself met with an encounter not of this age and spoke all he knew without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Ji likewise felt he had met a ruler of a once-in-an-age kind and held nothing back in his counsel.

sentences.zh: 遇急難，勇氣奮發，計畫立定，人莫能測。

translations.literal: When encountering urgent peril, his courage flared; plans were settled at once, and no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: In moments of crisis his courage blazed forth; his plans were fixed in an instant, and none could fathom his mind.

sentences.zh: 暇則敷陳王道。

translations.literal: In leisure he would expound the kingly way.
translations.idiomatic: In quieter moments he expounded the kingly way of governance.

sentences.zh: 帝每恭己以聽，常呼為老先生而不名，曰：「吾子房也。

translations.literal: The emperor each time listened with respectful restraint, often calling him Old Sir without using his name, saying, "You are my Zifang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always listened with humble attentiveness, often addressing him as "Old Sir" rather than by name, and said, "You are my Zifang.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「數以孔子之言導予。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Again and again you guide me with the words of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Again and again you guide me with Confucius's teachings.

sentences.zh: 」顧帷幄語秘莫能詳，而世所傳為神奇，多陰陽風角之說，非其至也。

translations.literal: " As for the secret words within the tent, none can know them in detail; what the world transmits as miraculous is mostly talk of yin-yang and wind angles—not his ultimate achievement.
translations.idiomatic: " The secret counsel exchanged within the imperial tent cannot be known in full; what the world celebrates as miraculous is mostly lore of yin-yang divination and wind omens—not the true measure of the man.

sentences.zh: 所為文章，氣昌而奇，與宋濂並為一代之宗。

translations.literal: The writings he produced were vigorous in spirit and marvelous; with Song Lian he was patriarch of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were vigorous in spirit and striking in originality; together with Song Lian he stood as a master of his generation.

sentences.zh: 所著有《覆瓿集》，《犁眉公集》傳於世。

translations.literal: Works he authored include the Fuboji and the Limeigongji, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works include the Fuboji and the Limeigongji, which have been handed down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 子璉、璟。

translations.literal: His sons were Lian and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Lian and Jing.

sentences.zh: 子 璉

translations.literal: Son: Lian
translations.idiomatic: Son: Lian

sentences.zh: 璉，字孟藻，有文行。

translations.literal: Lian, styled Mengzao, had literary accomplishment and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, whose courtesy name was Mengzao, was accomplished in letters and upright in conduct.

sentences.zh: 洪武十年授考功監丞，試監察御史，出為江西參政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongwu he was made vice director of the Bureau of Appointments, tried as investigating censor, and sent out as administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Hongwu he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Appointments, served a trial posting as investigating censor, and was then sent out as administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 太祖常欲大用之，為惟庸黨所脅，墮井死。

translations.literal: Taizu often wished to employ him greatly, but he was coerced by Weiyong's faction and fell into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had often wished to promote him to high office, but he was hounded by Hu Weiyong's faction and died after falling into a well.

sentences.zh: 璉子畾，字士端，洪武二十四年三月嗣伯，食祿五百石。

translations.literal: Lian's son Lei, styled Shiduan, in the third month of the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu succeeded to the marquisate with a stipend of five hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Lian's son Lei, whose courtesy name was Shiduan, succeeded to the marquisate in the third month of the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu with a stipend of five hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 初，基爵止及身，至是帝追念基功，又憫基父子皆為惟庸所厄，命增其祿，予世襲。

translations.literal: Earlier Ji's enfeoffment extended only to his person; now the emperor recalled Ji's merit and pitied that father and son had both been beset by Weiyong, ordering his stipend increased and granting hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ji's enfeoffment had been limited to his own lifetime; now the emperor, recalling Ji's achievements and grieving that both father and son had been persecuted by Weiyong, ordered an increase in the stipend and granted hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 明年坐事貶秩歸裏。

translations.literal: The next year, implicated in an affair, he was demoted in rank and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was implicated in a case, demoted in rank, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，坐事戍甘肅，尋赦還。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu, implicated in an affair, he was banished to garrison Gansu; soon he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Hongwu reign he was implicated in a case and banished to garrison duty in Gansu; he was soon pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 建文帝及成祖皆欲用之，以奉親守墓力辭。

translations.literal: Both the Jianwen Emperor and Chengzu wished to employ him; he firmly declined on the grounds of caring for his parent and guarding the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Jianwen Emperor and the Yongle Emperor wished to employ him, but he firmly declined on the grounds of caring for his parents and guarding the family tomb.

sentences.zh: 永樂間卒，子法停襲。

translations.literal: He died during Yongle; his son Fa's succession was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yongle reign; his son Fa's succession to the title was suspended.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年命錄基後，授法曾孫祿世襲《五經》博士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai an order recorded Ji's descendants; Fa's great-great-grandson Lu was granted hereditary succession as Doctor of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai the court recorded Ji's descendants; Fa's great-great-grandson Lu was granted hereditary appointment as Doctor of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年以給事中吳士偉言，乃命祿孫瑜為處州衛指揮使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi, on the words of supervising secretary Wu Shiwei, Lu's grandson Yu was appointed commander of Chuzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi, on the recommendation of supervising secretary Wu Shiwei, Lu's grandson Yu was appointed commander of Chuzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 正德八年加贈基太師，諡文成。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengde Ji was posthumously advanced to Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhengde Liu Ji was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，刑部郎中李瑜言，基宜侑享高廟，封世爵，如中山王達。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, Bureau Director Li Yu of the Ministry of Punishments said Ji should receive associated sacrifice in the High Temple and a hereditary enfeoffment, like Zhongshan Wang Da.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiajing, Bureau Director Li Yu of the Ministry of Punishments proposed that Liu Ji should receive associated sacrifice in the dynastic temple and a hereditary enfeoffment, as had been granted to Xu Da, Prince of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣議，僉言：「高帝收攬賢豪，一時佐命功臣並軌宣猷。

translations.literal: It was sent down for court discussion; all said, "The High Emperor gathered worthy heroes; the founding assistants of the age all walked the same path in proclaiming their plans.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the court for discussion; the officials unanimously stated, "The founding emperor gathered the empire's finest men, and the meritorious officials who aided him at the founding all served with comparable distinction.

sentences.zh: 而帷幄奇謀，中原大計，往往屬基，故在軍有子房之稱，剖符發諸葛之喻。

translations.literal: Yet stratagems within the tent and great plans for the Central Plains often fell to Ji; hence in the army he was called Zifang, and when the tally was cut the Zhuge analogy was invoked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the brilliant stratagems devised within the command tent and the grand plans for the Central Plains often fell to Ji; hence in military affairs he was called the Zifang of the age, and when enfeoffment was granted the Zhuge Liang analogy was invoked.

sentences.zh: 基亡之後，孫廌實嗣，太祖召諭再三，鐵券丹書，誓言世祿。

translations.literal: After Ji's death his grandson Guang actually succeeded; Taizu summoned and instructed him again and again, with iron certificate and cinnabar writing, swearing stipend for generations.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji's death his grandson Guang succeeded in fact; Taizu summoned and admonished him repeatedly, granting an iron certificate inscribed in cinnabar ink and swearing that the stipend would pass down through generations.

sentences.zh: 畾嗣未幾，旋即隕世，褫圭裳於末裔，委帶礪於空言。

translations.literal: Lei succeeded not long and soon perished; the jade regalia was stripped from later descendants, and belt and whetstone were left as empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Lei succeeded but soon died; the jade regalia was stripped from later descendants, and the promises of belt and whetstone proved hollow words.

sentences.zh: 或謂後嗣孤貧，弗克負荷；

translations.literal: Some said the later heirs were isolated and poor and could not bear the burden;
translations.idiomatic: Some said the later heirs were isolated and impoverished and could not bear the burden;

sentences.zh: 或謂長陵紹統，遂至猜嫌。

translations.literal: some said that when Changling inherited the succession, suspicion arose.
translations.idiomatic: others said that when the Yongle Emperor succeeded to the throne, suspicion arose.

sentences.zh: 雖一辱泥塗，傳聞多謬，而載書盟府，績效具存。

translations.literal: Though once disgraced in the mire and many rumors were false, the records in the covenant house and achievements all remain.
translations.idiomatic: Though the family once fell into disgrace and many rumors proved false, the records preserved in the archives of enfeoffment and their achievements remain fully documented.

sentences.zh: 昔武王興滅，天下歸心，成季無後，君子所歎。

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu raised the fallen; all under Heaven turned their hearts; when Chengjì had no heir, the gentleman sighed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity King Wu of Zhou restored fallen states and won the hearts of the realm; when Chengjì was left without heirs, the noble-minded lamented it.

sentences.zh: 基宜侑享太廟，其九世孫瑜宜嗣伯爵，與世襲。

translations.literal: Ji should receive associated sacrifice in the Grand Temple; his ninth-generation descendant Yu should succeed to the earldom, with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji should receive associated sacrifice in the Grand Temple; his ninth-generation descendant Yu should succeed to the earldom with hereditary transmission.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The decree said, "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The imperial rescript read, "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」瑜卒，孫世延嗣。

translations.literal: " Yu died; his grandson Shiyuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yu died, his grandson Shiyuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，南京振武營兵變，世延掌右軍都督府事，撫定之。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiajing, the Zhenwu camp at Nanjing mutinied; Shiyuan managed affairs of the Right Military Commission and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiajing reign, soldiers of the Zhenwu camp at Nanjing mutinied; Shiyuan, then managing affairs of the Right Military Commission, pacified them.

sentences.zh: 數上封事，不報，忿而恣橫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted sealed memorials and received no response; in anger he acted willfully and overbearingly.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted sealed memorials to the throne without response, and in resentment turned arrogant and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十四年，坐罪論死，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Wanli, convicted of a crime he was sentenced to death and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Wanli he was convicted of a crime, sentenced to death, and died.

sentences.zh: 適孫萊臣年幼，庶兄蓋臣借襲。

translations.literal: His proper grandson Laichen was young; a son of a concubine, Gaichen, borrowed the succession.
translations.idiomatic: His rightful grandson Laichen was still young, so a son born to a concubine, Gaichen, held the title in his stead.

sentences.zh: 蓋臣卒，萊臣當襲，蓋臣子孔昭復據之。

translations.literal: When Gaichen died, Laichen should have succeeded; Gaichen's son Kongzhao again seized it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaichen died, Laichen should have succeeded, but Gaichen's son Kongzhao seized the title again.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，出督南京操江，福王之立，與馬士英、阮大鋮比，後航海不知所終。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he went out to supervise the Yangzi patrol at Nanjing; when the Prince of Fu was established, he sided with Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng, and later sailed the sea with no known end.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was sent to supervise the Yangzi patrol at Nanjing; when the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he allied himself with Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng, and later put to sea, his final fate unknown.

sentences.zh: 子 璟

translations.literal: Son: Jing
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jing

sentences.zh: 璟，字仲璟，基次子，弱冠通諸經。

translations.literal: Jing, styled Zhongjing, was Ji's second son; at the capping age he was versed in all the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, whose courtesy name was Zhongjing, was Ji's second son; by the time he came of age he had mastered all the classics.

sentences.zh: 太祖念基，每歲召璟同章溢子允載、葉琛子永道、胡深子伯機，入見便殿，燕語如家人。

translations.literal: Taizu, remembering Ji, each year summoned Jing together with Zhang Yi's son Yunkai, Ye Chen's son Yongdao, and Hu Shen's son Boji to audience in the informal hall, conversing familiarly like family.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, remembering Ji, each year summoned Jing together with Zhang Yi's son Yunkai, Ye Chen's son Yongdao, and Hu Shen's son Boji to the informal palace hall, where they conversed as familiarly as family.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十三年命襲父爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Hongwu he was ordered to succeed to his father's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Hongwu he was ordered to succeed to his father's title.

sentences.zh: 璟言有長兄子廌在。

translations.literal: Jing said there was his elder brother's son Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pointed out that his elder brother's son Guang was still living.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，命廌襲封，以璟為閤門使，且諭之曰：「考宋制，閤門使即儀禮司。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, ordered Guang to succeed to the enfeoffment, and made Jing gate commissioner, instructing him, "Examining the Song system, the gate commissioner is the office of ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, ordered Guang to succeed to the title, and appointed Jing gate commissioner, telling him, "Under the Song system, the gate commissioner corresponds to the office of ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 朕欲汝日夕左右，以宣達為職，不特禮儀也。

translations.literal: I wish you day and night at my side, with conveying and announcing as your duty—not only ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I want you at my side day and night, charged with conveying my wishes—not merely with ceremonial duties.

sentences.zh: 」帝臨朝，出侍班，百官奏事有闕遺者，隨時糾正。

translations.literal: " When the emperor held court, Jing went out to attend in the ranks; when officials memorialized with omissions, he corrected them at once.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor held court, Jing stood in attendance with the officials; whenever a memorial contained omissions or errors, he corrected them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 都御史袁泰奏車牛事失實，帝宥之，泰忘引謝。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai memorialized on oxen for carts with facts not true; the emperor pardoned him, but Tai forgot to withdraw and apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai submitted a memorial on cart oxen that contained false statements; the emperor pardoned him, but Yuan forgot to withdraw and apologize.

sentences.zh: 璟糾之，服罪。

translations.literal: Jing rebuked him, and he confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Jing rebuked him on the spot, and the man admitted his fault.

sentences.zh: 帝因諭璟：「凡似此者，即面糾，朕雖不之罪，要令知朝廷綱紀。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon instructed Jing: "Whenever there are cases like this, rebuke them to their faces. Though I shall not punish them, it is necessary to make them know the discipline of the court."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then told Jing, "Whenever you see conduct like this, call it out to the man's face. I may not punish him myself, but he must learn that the court has its standards."

sentences.zh: 」己，復令同法司錄獄囚冤滯。

translations.literal: " Afterward, he again ordered him to join the judicial offices in reviewing prisoners whose cases were unjustly delayed.
translations.idiomatic: After that, he also ordered Jing to work with the judicial offices in reviewing prisoners whose cases had been wrongly held up.

sentences.zh: 谷王就封，擢為左長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Gu went to his fief, [Jing] was promoted to Left Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gu took up his enfeoffment, Jing was promoted to Left Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 璟論說英侃，喜談兵。

translations.literal: Jing was eloquent in discourse, heroic and upright, and loved to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was a forceful, forthright speaker and loved to talk of military matters.

sentences.zh: 初，溫州賊葉丁香叛，延安侯唐勝宗討之，決策於璟。

translations.literal: Initially, the bandit Ye Dingxiang rebelled at Wenzhou; the Marquis of Yan'an, Tang Shengzong, was sent to suppress him and made his strategic decisions through Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the bandit Ye Dingxiang rose in rebellion at Wenzhou, the Marquis of Yan'an, Tang Shengzong, was sent to put him down and relied on Jing for every major decision.

sentences.zh: 破賊還，稱璟才略。

translations.literal: After defeating the bandits and returning, he praised Jing's talent and strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned victorious, he praised Jing's talent and strategic skill.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「璟真伯溫兒矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "Jing is truly Boyou's son."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said delightedly, "Jing is truly Boyou's son."

sentences.zh: 」嘗與成祖弈，成祖曰：「卿不少讓耶？

translations.literal: " Once he played weiqi with Chengzu, who said: "Do you not yield even a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, playing weiqi with Chengzu, he heard the prince say, "Do you never give way at all?"

sentences.zh: 」璟正色曰：「可讓處則讓，不可讓者不敢讓也。

translations.literal: " Jing said with a stern face: "Where yielding is proper, I yield; where it is not proper, I dare not yield."
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered gravely, "Where yielding is right, I yield; where it is not, I dare not."

sentences.zh: 」成祖默然。

translations.literal: " Chengzu fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu said nothing.

sentences.zh: 靖難兵起，璟隨谷王歸京師，獻十六策，不聽。

translations.literal: When the Jingnan campaign began, Jing followed the Prince of Gu back to the capital, submitted sixteen stratagems, and was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingnan war broke out, Jing followed the Prince of Gu to the capital and offered sixteen plans of action, but they were ignored.

sentences.zh: 令參李景隆軍事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to participate in Li Jinglong's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve on Li Jinglong's staff.

sentences.zh: 景隆敗，璟夜渡盧溝河，冰裂馬陷，冒雪行三十里。

translations.literal: When Jinglong was defeated, Jing crossed the Lugou River at night; the ice broke and his horse fell in, and he traveled thirty li through the snow.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinglong's defeat, Jing crossed the Lugou River by night; the ice gave way and his horse went down, yet he pressed on through the snow for thirty li.

sentences.zh: 子貊自大同赴難，遇之良鄉，與俱歸。

translations.literal: His son Mo came from Datong to join the cause, met him at Liangxiang, and returned together with him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo had set out from Datong to join the struggle; they met at Liangxiang and went home together.

sentences.zh: 上《聞見錄》，不省，遂歸裏。

translations.literal: He submitted the "Records of What I Heard and Saw"; [the court] took no notice, and so he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his Records of What I Heard and Saw, but the court paid no attention, and he retired to his home district.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，召璟，稱疾不至。

translations.literal: When Chengzu ascended the throne, he summoned Jing, who claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzu took the throne, he summoned Jing, who pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 逮入京，猶稱殿下。

translations.literal: When seized and brought to the capital, he still addressed [Chengzu] as "Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: When he was seized and brought to the capital, he still addressed Chengzu as "Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 且云：「殿下百世後，逃不得一『篡』字。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "A hundred generations hence, Your Highness will not escape the word 'usurper.'"
translations.idiomatic: He went further and said, "A hundred generations from now, Your Highness will not escape the word usurper."

sentences.zh: 」下獄，自經死。

translations.literal: " He was imprisoned and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrown into prison and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 法官希旨，緣坐其家。

translations.literal: The judges, seeking to please [Chengzu], wished to extend punishment to his family.
translations.idiomatic: The judges, eager to please the throne, sought to punish his family as well.

sentences.zh: 成祖以基故，不許。

translations.literal: Chengzu, for Ji's sake, would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: For Ji's sake, Chengzu would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年授貊刑部照磨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, Mo was appointed Corrector in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xuande reign, Mo was appointed a corrector in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 宋濂，字景濂，其先金華之潛溪人，至濂乃遷浦江。

translations.literal: Song Lian, courtesy name Jinglian, his ancestors were from Qianxi in Jinhua; by Lian's time the family had moved to Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lian, styled Jinglian, came from a family originally of Qianxi in Jinhua; by his generation they had moved to Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 幼英敏強記，就學于聞人夢吉，通《五經》，復往從吳萊學。

translations.literal: In youth he was intelligent and had a powerful memory; he studied under Wenren Mengji, mastered the Five Classics, and then went to study under Wu Lai.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick and had an extraordinary memory. He studied under Wenren Mengji until he had mastered the Five Classics, then went on to learn from Wu Lai.

sentences.zh: 已，游柳貫、黃溍之門，兩人皆亟遜濂，自謂弗如。

translations.literal: Later he visited the schools of Liu Guan and Huang Jin; both men repeatedly deferred to Lian and declared themselves his inferiors.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered the circles of Liu Guan and Huang Jin, and both men repeatedly yielded place to him, saying they were not his equal.

sentences.zh: 元至正中，薦授翰林編修，以親老辭不行，入龍門山著書。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng reign of the Yuan, he was recommended and appointed Hanlin Compiler, but declined on account of aged parents and did not take office; he entered Longmen Mountain to write books.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan Zhizheng era he was recommended for appointment as a Hanlin compiler, but declined because his parents were old and withdrew instead to Longmen Mountain to write.

sentences.zh: 逾十餘年，太祖取婺州，召見濂。

translations.literal: More than ten years later, Taizu took Wuzhou and summoned Lian to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years passed before Taizu captured Wuzhou and summoned Lian to court.

sentences.zh: 時已改寧越府，命知府王顯宗開郡學，因以濂及葉儀為《五經》師。

translations.literal: By then it had been renamed Ningyue Prefecture; the prefect Wang Xianzong was ordered to establish a prefectural school, and Lian and Ye Yi were appointed as teachers of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: The place had by then been renamed Ningyue Prefecture. The prefect Wang Xianzong was ordered to open a prefectural school, and Lian and Ye Yi were made instructors in the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，以李善長薦，與劉基、章、溢、葉琛並征至應天，除江南儒學提舉，命授太子經，尋改起居注。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, on Li Shanchang's recommendation, together with Liu Ji, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen he was summoned to Yingtian, appointed Commissioner for Confucian Schools in Jiangnan, ordered to instruct the Crown Prince in the classics, and soon transferred to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, on Li Shanchang's recommendation, he was summoned to Yingtian together with Liu Ji, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen. He was appointed Commissioner for Confucian Schools in Jiangnan, charged with instructing the Crown Prince in the classics, and soon afterward made a diarist.

sentences.zh: 濂長基一歲，皆起東南，負重名。

translations.literal: Lian was one year older than Ji; both had risen from the southeast and bore great reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was a year older than Ji. Both had come up from the southeast and carried great renown.

sentences.zh: 基雄邁有奇氣，而濂自命儒者。

translations.literal: Ji was bold and possessed an unusual spirit, while Lian styled himself a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was bold and charged with an uncommon force of character, whereas Lian thought of himself above all as a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 基佐軍中謀議，濂亦首用文學受知，恒侍左右，備顧問。

translations.literal: Ji assisted with counsel in the army; Lian likewise first gained recognition through literary learning, constantly attending at [Taizu's] side as adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Ji advised on military plans, while Lian won favor first through his learning. He was constantly at Taizu's side, ready to answer whenever he was consulted.

sentences.zh: 嘗召講《春秋左氏傳》，濂進曰：「《春秋》乃孔子褒善貶惡之書，苟能遵行，則賞罰適中，天下可定也。

translations.literal: Once [Taizu] summoned him to expound on the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; Lian submitted: "The Spring and Autumn Annals is Confucius's book for praising the good and condemning the evil; if one can follow it, rewards and punishments will be appropriate and the realm can be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu called him in to lecture on the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals. Lian said, "The Spring and Autumn Annals is Confucius's book for honoring the good and condemning the wicked. If Your Majesty can follow it, rewards and punishments will fall where they should and the realm can be brought to order."

sentences.zh: 」太祖禦端門，口釋黃石公《三略》。

translations.literal: " Taizu addressed the Duan Gate and orally expounded the Three Strategies of Lord Yellow Stone.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took his place at the Duan Gate and began reciting from the Three Strategies of Lord Yellow Stone.

sentences.zh: 濂曰：「《尚書》二《典》、三《謨》，帝王大經大法畢具，願留意講明之。

translations.literal: Lian said: "In the Documents, the two Canons and three Counsels contain in full the great principles and laws of emperors and kings; I hope Your Majesty will take care to study and clarify them."
translations.idiomatic: Lian said, "In the Documents, the two Canons and three Counsels set out in full the great principles by which emperors and kings should rule. I hope Your Majesty will give careful thought to studying them."

sentences.zh: 」已，論賞賚，復曰：「得天下以人心為本。

translations.literal: " Later, when discussing rewards and gifts, he again said: "Gaining the realm depends on winning people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the talk turned to rewards and gifts, he added, "Winning the realm depends on winning people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 人心不固，雖金帛充牣，將焉用之。

translations.literal: If hearts are not secure, though gold and silk fill the storehouses, of what use will they be?
translations.idiomatic: If hearts are not secure, what good will it do to fill the treasuries with gold and silk?

sentences.zh: 」太祖悉稱善。

translations.literal: " Taizu fully approved.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu approved of everything he said.

sentences.zh: 乙巳三月，乞歸省。

translations.literal: In the third month of yisi, he requested leave to visit his family.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the yisi cycle, he asked leave to go home and visit his family.

sentences.zh: 太祖與太子並加勞賜。

translations.literal: Taizu and the Crown Prince both sent him gifts of encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and the Crown Prince both sent him gifts and words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 濂上箋謝，並奉書太子，勉以孝友敬恭、進德修業。

translations.literal: Lian submitted a memorial of thanks and also sent the Crown Prince a letter urging filial piety, brotherly affection, respect, and diligent cultivation of virtue and accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lian submitted a memorial of thanks and also wrote to the Crown Prince, urging filial piety, brotherly affection, reverence, and steady progress in virtue and learning.

sentences.zh: 太祖覽書大悅，召太子，為語書意，賜劄褒答，並令太子致書報焉。

translations.literal: Taizu read the letter with great delight, summoned the Crown Prince, explained the letter's meaning to him, bestowed a written commendation in reply, and also ordered the Crown Prince to send a letter in response.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu read the letter with great pleasure, summoned the Crown Prince, explained its meaning to him, sent Lian a letter of praise in reply, and ordered the prince to write back as well.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he mourned his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服除，召還。

translations.literal: When his mourning period ended, he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was over, he was summoned back to court.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年詔修元史，命充總裁官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu an edict ordered the compilation of the History of Yuan; he was appointed chief editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongwu an edict ordered the compilation of the History of Yuan, and he was appointed chief editor.

sentences.zh: 是年八月史成，除翰林院學士。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month the history was completed, and he was appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The history was finished that eighth month, and he was appointed a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，儒士歐陽佑等采故元元統以後事蹟還朝，仍命濂等續修，六越月再成，賜金帛。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, the Confucian scholar Ouyang You and others returned to court after collecting accounts of events from after the Yuantong period of the former Yuan; Lian and others were again ordered to continue the compilation; in six months it was completed again, and they were granted gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year the scholar Ouyang You and others returned to court after gathering material on events from the Yuantong period onward under the former Yuan. Lian and the others were ordered to continue the work; six months later it was finished again, and they were rewarded with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 是月，以失朝參，降編修。

translations.literal: That month, for missing court attendance, he was demoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was demoted to compiler for missing court audience.

sentences.zh: 四年遷國子司業，坐考祀孔子禮不以時奏，謫安遠知縣，旋召為禮部主事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; for failing to memorialize the ceremony of sacrificing to Confucius on time during an examination, he was demoted to magistrate of Anyuan, but was soon recalled as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, but during an examination he failed to report the ceremony for sacrificing to Confucius on time and was banished to serve as magistrate of Anyuan. He was soon recalled and appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年遷贊善大夫。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝留意文治，徵召四方儒士張唯等數十人，擇其年少俊異者，皆擢編修，令入禁中文華堂肄業，命濂為之師。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor paid attention to literary governance, summoning several dozen Confucian scholars from all quarters such as Zhang Wei; those among them who were young and outstanding were all promoted to compilers and ordered to study in the Wenhua Hall within the Forbidden City, with Lian appointed as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Emperor turned his mind to civil governance.
