He summoned several dozen scholars from across the realm, including Zhang Wei, chose out the young and exceptionally talented among them, promoted them all to compilers, and had them study in the Wenhua Hall inside the Forbidden City with Lian as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 濂傅太子先後十餘年，凡一言動，皆以禮法諷勸，使歸於道，至有關政教及前代興亡事，必拱手曰：「當如是，不當如彼。

translations.literal: Lian tutored the Crown Prince for more than ten years in all; in every word and action he admonished him with ritual and law to bring him back to the Way; whenever matters touched on government, teaching, or the rise and fall of former dynasties, he would invariably bow with hands clasped and say: "One should act thus; one should not act thus."
translations.idiomatic: Lian instructed the Crown Prince for more than ten years in all. In every word and deed he gently admonished him with ritual and law and tried to bring him back to the right path. Whenever the subject touched government, moral teaching, or the rise and fall of earlier dynasties, he would bow with clasped hands and say, "This is how it should be done; that is how it should not."

sentences.zh: 」皇太子每斂容嘉納，言必稱師父雲。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince always composed himself and accepted it gladly, and in speech invariably referred to his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince always composed himself and accepted the advice gladly; in conversation he unfailingly spoke of what his teacher had said.

sentences.zh: 帝剖符封功臣，召濂議五等封爵。

translations.literal: When the Emperor divided the tally and enfeoffed meritorious ministers, he summoned Lian to discuss the five ranks of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor broke the seals and enfeoffed his meritorious ministers, he summoned Lian to discuss the five ranks of nobility.

sentences.zh: 宿大本堂，討論達旦，曆據漢、唐故實，量其中而奏之。

translations.literal: He stayed overnight in the Hall of Great Foundation; they discussed until dawn, citing precedents from Han and Tang throughout, weighed the mean among them, and memorialized the result.
translations.idiomatic: Lian stayed overnight in the Hall of Great Foundation, and they debated until dawn, drawing on precedents from Han and Tang, weighing the balance among them, and then memorializing what they had decided.

sentences.zh: 甘露屢降，帝問災祥之故。

translations.literal: Sweet dew repeatedly fell; the Emperor asked the reason for such omens of fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: When sweet dew fell again and again, the Emperor asked what such omens of fortune and misfortune meant.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「受命不于天，於其人，休符不于祥，於其仁。

translations.literal: He replied: "Receiving the mandate lies not in Heaven but in the person; auspicious tokens lie not in omens but in benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Receiving the Mandate does not depend on Heaven but on the man; true signs of favor do not lie in portents but in benevolence."

sentences.zh: 《春秋》書異不書祥，為是故也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records anomalies but not auspicious signs - for this very reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Spring and Autumn Annals records anomalies but not auspicious omens.

sentences.zh: 」皇從子文正得罪，濂曰：「文正固當死，陛下體親親之誼，置諸遠地則善矣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's cousin Wen Zheng was convicted of a crime; Lian said: "Wen Zheng indeed deserved death, but if Your Majesty would honor the affection due kin and banish him to a distant place, that would be well."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor's cousin Wen Zheng was found guilty of a crime, Lian said, "Wen Zheng truly deserved death, but if Your Majesty would honor the bonds of kinship and send him to a distant place instead, that would be the better course."

sentences.zh: 」車駕祀方丘，患心不甯，濂從容言曰：「養心莫善於寡欲，審能行之，則心清而身泰矣。

translations.literal: " When the imperial carriage performed sacrifice at the Square Altar, the Emperor suffered restless heart; Lian said calmly: "In nourishing the heart nothing is better than few desires; if Your Majesty can truly practice this, the heart will be clear and the body at ease."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went to sacrifice at the Square Altar, the Emperor was troubled by palpitations. Lian said calmly, "Nothing nourishes the heart better than limiting one's desires. If Your Majesty can truly put that into practice, the heart will grow clear and the body find peace."

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善者良久。

translations.literal: " The Emperor expressed approval for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor expressed his approval at length.

sentences.zh: 嘗問以帝王之學，何書為要。

translations.literal: Once [Taizu] asked what book was most important for the learning of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu asked which book was most essential to the learning of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 濂舉《大學衍義》。

translations.literal: Lian named the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Lian named the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning.

sentences.zh: 乃命大書揭之殿兩廡壁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered it written large and posted on the walls of both wings of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then ordered the text copied out in large characters and hung on the walls of both wings of the hall.

sentences.zh: 頃之禦西廡，諸大臣皆在，帝指《衍義》中司馬遷論黃、老事，命濂講析。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward [Taizu] attended the west wing; all the great ministers were present; the Emperor pointed to Sima Qian's discussion of Huang-Lao in the Extended Meaning and ordered Lian to explain and analyze it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Taizu went to the west wing with all the chief ministers in attendance. He pointed to Sima Qian's discussion of Huang-Lao in the Extended Meaning and ordered Lian to explain it.

sentences.zh: 講畢，因曰：「漢武溺方技謬悠之學，改文、景恭儉之風，民力既敝，然後嚴刑督之。

translations.literal: When the exposition was finished, [Lian] therefore said: "Emperor Wu of Han drowned himself in the frivolous learning of alchemical arts and occult arts, abandoning the respectful frugality of the Wen and Jing reigns; when the people's strength was already exhausted, he then enforced them with harsh punishments."
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, Lian went on, "Emperor Wu of Han drowned himself in the empty learning of alchemy and occult arts, turning away from the respectful frugality of the Wen and Jing reigns. Once the people's strength was spent, he drove them on with harsh punishments."

sentences.zh: 人主誠以禮義治心，則邪說不入，以學校治民，則禍亂不興，刑罰非所先也。

translations.literal: If a ruler truly governs his heart with ritual and righteousness, perverse doctrines will not enter; if he governs the people through schools, calamity and turmoil will not arise - punishments are not what should come first.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler truly governs his heart with ritual and righteousness, perverse doctrines cannot enter; if he governs the people through schools, disaster and rebellion will not arise. Punishment should never come first.

sentences.zh: 」問三代歷數及封疆廣狹，既備陳之，復曰：「三代治天下以仁義，故多歷年所。

translations.literal: " [Taizu] asked about the duration and the extent of territory of the Three Dynasties; after Lian had fully set them forth, he again said: "The Three Dynasties governed the realm with benevolence and righteousness, and therefore lasted many years."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked about the length of reign and the breadth of territory of the Three Dynasties. After Lian had laid it all out in detail, he added, "The Three Dynasties ruled the realm through benevolence and righteousness, and that is why they endured so long."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「三代以上，所讀何書？

translations.literal: " [Taizu] also asked: "Before the Three Dynasties, what books did people read?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked again, "Before the Three Dynasties, what books did people read?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「上古載籍未立，人不專講誦。

translations.literal: " [Lian] replied: "In high antiquity written records had not yet been established, and people did not devotedly recite texts."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In high antiquity written records had not yet been established, and people did not devote themselves to reciting texts."

sentences.zh: 君人者兼治教之責，率以躬行，則眾自化。

translations.literal: One who rules others bears the duty of both governance and teaching; if he leads through personal conduct, the multitude will transform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: One who rules others bears the double duty of governing and teaching. If he leads through his own conduct, the people will transform themselves.

sentences.zh: 」嘗奉制詠鷹，令七舉足即成，有「自古戒禽荒」之言。

translations.literal: " Once, by imperial command, he composed a poem on an eagle, required to complete it in seven paces, containing the phrase "Since ancient times one is warned against excess in hawking and hunting."
translations.idiomatic: Once, by imperial command, he composed a poem on an eagle and was required to finish it within seven paces. It contained the line, "Since ancient times men have been warned against the excesses of hawking and hunting."

sentences.zh: 帝忻然曰：「卿可謂善陳矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "You may truly be said to offer good remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said with pleasure, "You may truly be said to offer good remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 」濂之隨事納忠，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " Lian's loyal counsels on the affairs at hand were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Lian's loyal counsel on whatever came before him was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 六年七月遷侍講學士，知制誥，同修國史，兼贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was transferred to Lecturing Academician, Director of Edicts, co-compiler of the dynastic history, and concurrently Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was made Lecturing Academician, Director of Edicts, co-compiler of the dynastic history, and concurrently Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 命與詹同、樂韶鳳修日曆，又與吳伯宗等修寶訓。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Zhan Tong and Yue Shaofeng to compile the calendar, and also with Wu Bozong and others to compile the Precious Instructions.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the calendar with Zhan Tong and Yue Shaofeng, and the Precious Instructions with Wu Bozong and others.

sentences.zh: 九月定散官資階，給濂中順大夫，欲任以政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month civil official ranks were fixed; Lian was given the rank of Middle Grand Master of Court, and [the Emperor] wished to entrust him with administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the civil ranks were fixed, and Lian was given the rank of Middle Grand Master of Court. The Emperor wished to put him in charge of affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「臣無他長，待罪禁近足矣。

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "Your subject has no other special talent; serving near the throne in my present post is sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "Your subject has no other special talent; serving close to the throne in my present post is enough."

sentences.zh: 」帝益重之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor respected him all the more.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，從太子及秦、晉、楚、靖江四王講武中都。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year he accompanied the Crown Prince and the four princes of Qin, Jin, Chu, and Jingjiang to military exercises in the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year he accompanied the Crown Prince and the four princes of Qin, Jin, Chu, and Jingjiang to military exercises at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 帝得輿圖《濠梁古跡》一卷，遣使賜太子，題其外，令濂詢訪，隨處言之。

translations.literal: The Emperor obtained a scroll of maps titled "Ancient Sites at Haoliang," sent an envoy to gift it to the Crown Prince, inscribed the outside, and ordered Lian to inquire and explain, speaking of each place as they passed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor obtained a scroll of maps called Ancient Sites at Haoliang, sent an envoy to present it to the Crown Prince, wrote an inscription on the cover, and ordered Lian to inquire into each place and explain it as they came to it.

sentences.zh: 太子以示濂，因歷歷舉陳，隨事進說，甚有規益。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince showed it to Lian, who thereupon set forth each site in detail, offering instruction on each matter as they went - very much to beneficial regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince showed it to Lian, who then went through each site in turn, offering instruction on each matter as they went. The lessons were of great benefit.

sentences.zh: 濂性誠謹，官內庭久，未嘗訐人過。

translations.literal: Lian's nature was sincere and cautious; having served long in the inner court, he never exposed others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was sincere and cautious by nature. After long service in the inner court, he never exposed another man's faults.

sentences.zh: 所居室，署「溫樹」。

translations.literal: His residence bore the inscription "Warm Tree."
translations.idiomatic: On the house where he lived he posted the words "Warm Tree."

sentences.zh: 客問禁中語，即指示之。

translations.literal: When guests asked about affairs within the Forbidden City, he would point to the inscription.
translations.idiomatic: When guests asked about affairs within the Forbidden City, he would simply point to the inscription.

sentences.zh: 嘗與客飲，帝密使人偵視。

translations.literal: Once he drank with a guest; the Emperor secretly sent someone to spy on them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he was drinking with a guest, the Emperor secretly sent someone to watch them.

sentences.zh: 翼日，問濂昨飲酒否，坐客為誰，饌何物。

translations.literal: The next day [the Emperor] asked whether Lian had drunk wine yesterday, who the guests were, and what the food had been.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he asked whether Lian had drunk wine the day before, who had been present, and what had been served.

sentences.zh: 濂具以實對。

translations.literal: Lian answered completely and truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Lian answered in full and truthfully.

sentences.zh: 笑曰：「誠然，卿不朕欺。

translations.literal: [The Emperor] laughed and said: "It is indeed so - you did not deceive me."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and said, "It is exactly so. You did not deceive me."

sentences.zh: 」間召問群臣臧否，濂惟舉其善者曰：「善者與臣友，臣知之；

translations.literal: " Occasionally summoned to be asked about the merits and faults of ministers, Lian would mention only their good points, saying: "Those who are good are my friends; I know them;"
translations.idiomatic: From time to time, when summoned and asked about the merits and faults of the ministers, Lian would mention only their good qualities, saying, "Those who are good are my friends, and I know them;

sentences.zh: 其不善者，不能知也。

translations.literal: as for those who are not good, I cannot know them.
translations.idiomatic: as for those who are not good, I have no knowledge of them."

sentences.zh: 」主事茹太素上書萬餘言。

translations.literal: " Principal Clerk Ru Taisu submitted a memorial of more than ten thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: Principal Clerk Ru Taisu submitted a memorial of more than ten thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，問廷臣，或指其書曰：「此不敬，此誹謗非法。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and questioned the court ministers; some pointed to the memorial saying: "This is disrespect; this is slander and contrary to law."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and questioned the court ministers. Some pointed to passages in the memorial and said, "This is disrespectful; this is slander and unlawful."

sentences.zh: 」問濂，對曰：「彼盡忠于陛下耳。

translations.literal: " When he asked Lian, Lian replied: "He was wholly loyal to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: When he asked Lian, Lian answered, "He was wholly loyal to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 陛下方開言路，惡可深罪。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has just opened the path for frank speech - how can he be deeply punished?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just opened the way for frank speech. How can he be punished severely?"

sentences.zh: 」既而帝覽其書，有足采者。

translations.literal: " Later the Emperor read through the memorial and found points worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Emperor read through the memorial, he found much in it worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 悉召廷臣詰責，因呼濂字曰：「微景濂幾誤罪言者。

translations.literal: He summoned all the court ministers to rebuke them, and addressing Lian by his courtesy name said: "But for Jinglian, I would almost have wrongly punished the one who spoke."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned all the court ministers to rebuke them, then addressed Lian by his courtesy name and said, "But for Jinglian, I would almost have punished the man who spoke."

sentences.zh: 」於是帝廷譽之曰：「朕聞太上為聖，其次為賢，其次為君子。

translations.literal: " Thereupon in court the Emperor praised him, saying: "I have heard that the highest is a sage, next a worthy man, next a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Then, in open court, the Emperor praised him, saying, "I have heard that the highest rank is sage, the next worthy, and the next gentleman."

sentences.zh: 宋景濂事朕十九年，未嘗有一言之偽，誚一人之短，始終無二，非止君子，抑可謂賢矣。

translations.literal: Song Jinglian has served me for nineteen years, never once a false word, never once ridiculing another's fault; from beginning to end without duplicity - not merely a gentleman, he may truly be called a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jinglian has served me for nineteen years without once speaking falsely or once mocking another man's faults. He has been consistent from first to last. He is not merely a gentleman; he may truly be called a worthy man."

sentences.zh: 」每燕見，必設坐命茶，每旦必令侍膳，往復諮詢，常夜分乃罷。

translations.literal: " Whenever they met at private audience, he invariably had a seat set out and ordered tea; every morning he had Lian attend his meals; back and forth he questioned him, and often it was midnight before they parted.
translations.idiomatic: At every private audience, the Emperor always had a seat prepared and tea served. Every morning he had Lian dine with him, questioned him at length, and often did not let him go until the middle of the night.

sentences.zh: 濂不能飲，帝嘗強之至三觴，行不成步。

translations.literal: Lian could not drink; the Emperor once forced him to down three cups, and he could not walk straight.
translations.idiomatic: Lian could not hold his liquor. The Emperor once forced three cups on him, and Lian could barely keep his footing.

sentences.zh: 帝大歡樂。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly amused.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 禦制《楚辭》一章，命詞臣賦《醉學士詩》。

translations.literal: He imperially composed a chapter of "Songs of Chu" and ordered the literary ministers to compose "Poem of the Drunken Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally composed a chapter in the manner of "Songs of Chu" and ordered his literary ministers to write "Poem of the Drunken Scholar."

sentences.zh: 又嘗調甘露于湯，手酌以飲濂曰：「此能愈疾延年，願與卿共之。

translations.literal: He also once mixed sweet dew into soup, scooped it with his own hand to give Lian to drink, and said: "This can cure illness and prolong life; I wish to share it with you.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he mixed sweet dew into broth, ladled it out with his own hand for Lian to drink, and said, "This can cure illness and prolong life. I wish to share it with you.

sentences.zh: 」又詔太子賜濂良馬，復為制《白馬歌》一章，亦命侍臣和焉。

translations.literal: " He also ordered the Crown Prince to bestow a fine horse on Lian, again composed a chapter of "Song of the White Horse," and likewise ordered attendant ministers to compose matching pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Crown Prince to give Lian a fine horse, composed another piece, "Song of the White Horse," and had the attendant ministers compose matching poems.

sentences.zh: 其寵待如此。

translations.literal: His favor was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 九年進學士承旨知制誥，兼贊善如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Hanlin Academician Chancellor and Drafting Director for Edicts, continuing as Tutor as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the reign he was promoted to Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Director of Edict Drafting, while retaining his post as Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 其明年致仕，賜《禦制文集》及綺帛，問濂年幾何，曰：「六十有八。

translations.literal: The following year he retired from office; he was granted "Imperially Composed Collected Writings" and silks, and when asked how old Lian was, he replied: "Sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he retired. The Emperor granted him the "Imperially Composed Collected Writings" and bolts of silk, asked Lian his age, and Lian answered, "Sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃曰：「藏此綺三十二年，作百歲衣可也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then said: "Store this silk for thirty-two years, and it may be made into a garment for your hundredth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then said, "Store this silk for thirty-two years, and it can be made into a garment for your hundredth birthday.

sentences.zh: 」濂頓首謝。

translations.literal: " Lian bowed his head to the ground in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Lian kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 又明年，來朝。

translations.literal: The year after that, he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court again.

sentences.zh: 十三年，長孫慎坐胡惟庸黨，帝欲置濂死。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, his eldest grandson Shen was implicated in the Hu Weiyong faction; the Emperor wished to put Lian to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, his eldest grandson Shen was implicated in the Hu Weiyong conspiracy, and the Emperor intended to condemn Lian to death.

sentences.zh: 皇后太子力救，乃安置茂州。

translations.literal: The Empress and Crown Prince exerted themselves to save him, whereupon he was assigned to Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress and Crown Prince intervened strenuously on his behalf, and he was instead relegated to Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 濂狀貌豐偉，美須髯，視近而明，一黍上能作數字。

translations.literal: Lian's bearing was full and imposing, his beard and whiskers handsome; though his sight was nearsighted, it was keen — on the space of a single grain of millet he could write several characters.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was tall and imposing, with a fine beard. Though nearsighted, his eyes were sharp enough to write several characters on a space no larger than a grain of millet.

sentences.zh: 自少至老，未嘗一日去書卷，於學無所不通。

translations.literal: From youth to old age he never for a single day put aside his books; in learning there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he never spent a day without his books, and there was no branch of learning he did not command.

sentences.zh: 為文醇深演迤，與古作者並。

translations.literal: His writing was rich, deep, and flowing — on a par with the authors of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was rich, profound, and flowing, ranking him with the great writers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 在朝，郊社宗廟山川百神之典，朝會宴享律曆衣冠之制，四裔貢賦賞勞之儀，旁及元勳巨卿碑記刻石之辭，鹹以委濂，屢推為開國文臣之首。

translations.literal: At court, the rites of suburban sacrifice, ancestral temples, mountains and rivers, and the hundred spirits; the regulations for court assemblies, banquets, calendar and measurements, and robes and caps; the ceremonies for tribute, taxation, rewards, and service from the four quarters — as well as the inscriptions on steles and carved stones for founding meritorious ministers and great officials — all were entrusted to Lian, and he was repeatedly regarded as the foremost literary minister among the founders of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: At court, whether the rituals for suburban sacrifice, ancestral temples, mountains and rivers, and the host of spirits; the regulations governing assemblies, banquets, calendar, weights and measures, and ceremonial dress; the ceremonies for tribute, taxation, and reward from the four quarters; or the inscriptions for steles and stone monuments honoring founding ministers — all were entrusted to Lian, who was repeatedly acclaimed as the leading literary statesman of the founding generation.

sentences.zh: 士大夫造門乞文者，後先相踵。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials who came to his gate begging for compositions followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials came to his door seeking compositions in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 外國貢使亦知其名，數問宋先生起居無恙否。

translations.literal: Envoys from foreign states also knew his name and repeatedly asked whether Master Song was well.
translations.idiomatic: Even foreign tribute envoys knew his name and often inquired whether Master Song remained in good health.

sentences.zh: 高麗、安南、日本至出兼金購文集。

translations.literal: Korea, Annam, and Japan even offered double weight in gold to purchase his collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: Korea, Annam, and Japan paid double-weight gold to obtain his collected writings.

sentences.zh: 四方學者悉稱為「太史公」，不以姓氏。

translations.literal: Scholars everywhere uniformly called him "Grand Historian" without using his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars throughout the realm called him "Grand Historian" rather than by his surname.

sentences.zh: 雖白首侍從，其勳業爵位不逮基，而一代禮樂製作，濂所裁定者居多。

translations.literal: Although he attended the throne white-haired to the end, his achievements and noble rank did not match Ji's, yet of the rites, music, and institutional works of the age, Lian adjudicated the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served at the Emperor's side until his hair turned white, his achievements and ennoblement never equaled Liu Ji's; yet most of the age's rites, music, and institutional regulations were determined by Lian.

sentences.zh: 其明年，卒於夔，年七十二。

translations.literal: The following year he died at Kui, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died at Kui, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 知事葉以從葬之蓮花山下。

translations.literal: Magistrate Ye Cong buried him beneath Lotus Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Ye Cong had him buried at the foot of Lotus Mountain.

sentences.zh: 蜀獻王慕濂名，復移塋華陽城東。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu, admiring Lian's name, moved the grave again to the east of Huayang city.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu, admiring Lian's reputation, had the grave moved again to the east of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年，四川巡撫馬俊奏：「濂真儒翊運，述作可師，黼黻多功，輔導著績。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi, Sichuan Surveillance Commissioner Ma Jun memorialized: "Lian was a true Confucian who aided the founding of the dynasty, whose writings may serve as models; his ceremonial adornments brought many achievements, and his instruction left outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Hongzhi reign, Sichuan Surveillance Commissioner Ma Jun memorialized, "Lian was a true Confucian who aided the dynasty's rise; his writings are worthy of emulation; he contributed greatly to court ritual and dress, and his tutelage left a lasting record of merit.

sentences.zh: 久死遠戍，幽壤沉淪，乞加恤錄。

translations.literal: Long dead in distant exile, his buried remains sunk in obscurity — I beg that posthumous favor be granted and his record restored.
translations.idiomatic: He died long ago in distant exile, and his remains lie forgotten in an obscure grave. I beseech that posthumous honors be granted and his record restored.

sentences.zh: 」下禮部議，復其官，春秋祭葬所。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation; his office was restored, and sacrificial offerings at his grave were instituted in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Rites, which restored his official rank and established spring and autumn sacrifices at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 正德中，追諡文憲。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, he was posthumously given the title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign, he was posthumously honored with the title Wenvian.

sentences.zh: 仲子璲最知名，字仲珩，善詩，尤工書法。

translations.literal: His second son Qiong was the most renowned, styled Zhongheng; he excelled at poetry and was especially skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Qiong was the best known. Courtesy name Zhongheng, he was skilled at poetry and particularly accomplished in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，以濂故，召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongwu, on account of Lian, he was summoned and appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Hongwu, on account of Lian, Qiong was summoned and appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其兄子慎亦為儀禮序班。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Shen also served as an orderly in the Office of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Lian's nephew Shen also served as an orderly in the Office of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 帝數試璲與慎，並教誡之。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly tested Qiong and Shen, instructing and admonishing them both.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly tested Qiong and Shen, instructing and admonishing them.

sentences.zh: 笑語濂曰：「卿為朕教太子諸王，朕亦教卿子孫矣。

translations.literal: Laughing, he said to Lian: "You teach the Crown Prince and the princes for me — I, too, am teaching your descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Smiling, he said to Lian, "You instruct the Crown Prince and the princes for me; I, too, am instructing your descendants.

sentences.zh: 」濂行步艱，帝必命璲、慎扶掖之。

translations.literal: " When Lian's steps were labored, the Emperor invariably ordered Qiong and Shen to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lian walked with difficulty, the Emperor always ordered Qiong and Shen to assist him.

sentences.zh: 祖孫父子，共官內庭，眾以為榮。

translations.literal: Grandfather, grandson, and father and son all held office within the palace — the multitude regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather, grandson, father, and son all held posts within the palace, and many regarded it as a singular honor.

sentences.zh: 慎坐罪，璲亦連坐，並死，家屬悉徙茂州。

translations.literal: When Shen was convicted, Qiong was also implicated by association; both were executed, and all their family members were relocated to Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen was convicted, Qiong was punished as an associate. Both were executed, and all their families were exiled to Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 建文帝即位，追念濂興宗舊學，召璲子懌官翰林。

translations.literal: When the Jianwen Emperor ascended the throne, recalling Lian's old instruction of the heir apparent, he summoned Qiong's son Yi to an office in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen Emperor took the throne, remembering Lian's tutelage of the heir apparent, he summoned Qiong's son Yi to serve in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年，濂孫坐奸党鄭公智外親，詔特宥之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle, Lian's grandson was implicated as an in-law of the traitor Zheng Gongzhi; an edict specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongle, Lian's grandson was implicated through his connection to the traitor Zheng Gongzhi; an edict specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 葉琛，字景淵，麗水人。

translations.literal: Ye Chen, styled Jingyuan, was a native of Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Chen, courtesy name Jingyuan, was from Lishui.

sentences.zh: 博學有才藻。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and talented in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and gifted in composition.

sentences.zh: 元末從石抹宜孫守處州，為畫策，捕誅山寇，授行省元帥。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he followed Shimao Yisun in defending Chuzhou, devised stratagems, captured and executed mountain bandits, and was appointed Marshal of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan, he served under Shimao Yisun in the defense of Chuzhou, devised strategy, captured and executed mountain bandits, and was appointed Marshal of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王師下處州，琛避走建寧。

translations.literal: When the royal army descended on Chuzhou, Chen fled to Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army took Chuzhou, Chen fled to Jianning.

sentences.zh: 以薦征至應天，授營田司僉事。

translations.literal: Recommended, he was summoned to Yingtian and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Land-Reclamation Office.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was summoned to Yingtian and appointed Vice Commissioner in the Land-Reclamation Office.

sentences.zh: 尋遷洪都知府，佐鄧愈鎮守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Prefect of Hongdu to assist Deng Yu in garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Prefect of Hongdu, where he assisted Deng Yu in holding the city.

sentences.zh: 祝宗、康泰叛，愈脫走，琛被執，不屈，大罵，死之。

translations.literal: Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled; Yu escaped, but Chen was seized, refused to submit, cursed loudly, and died for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled, Deng Yu escaped, but Chen was captured. He refused to submit, cursed his captors, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 追封南陽郡侯，塑像耿再成祠，後祀功臣廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang; his image was placed in the shrine of Geng Zaicheng, and later he was honored in the Temple of Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang. His statue was placed in Geng Zaicheng's shrine, and later he was enrolled among the meritorious ministers in the dynastic temple.

sentences.zh: 章溢，字三益，龍泉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Sanyi, was a native of Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Sanyi, was from Longquan.

sentences.zh: 始生，聲如鐘。

translations.literal: At birth, his voice was like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born, his cry sounded like a bell.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，與胡深同師王毅。

translations.literal: At twenty, he and Hu Shen shared Wang Yi as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he studied under Wang Yi together with Hu Shen.

sentences.zh: 毅，字叔剛，許謙門人也，教授鄉里，講解經義，聞者多感悟。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Shugang, was a disciple of Xu Qian; he taught in his native district, expounding the meaning of the classics, and many who heard him were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, courtesy name Shugang, was a disciple of Xu Qian. He taught in his home district, lecturing on the classics in such a way that many listeners were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 溢從之游，同志聖賢學，天性孝友。

translations.literal: Yi studied under him, sharing the ambition to pursue the learning of the sages, his nature filial and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi studied with him, embracing the same aim of pursuing sage learning, and was by nature filial and dutiful toward his kin.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊金華，元憲使禿堅不花禮之，改官秦中，要與俱行。

translations.literal: Once when traveling in Jinhua, Yuan Commissioner Toghan Bukha treated him with ceremony, transferred his office to Qinzhong, and pressed him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Once while traveling in Jinhua, the Yuan Commissioner Toghan Bukha received him with full honors, transferred his appointment to Qinzhong, and insisted that he accompany him.

sentences.zh: 至虎林，心動，辭歸。

translations.literal: Reaching Hulin, his heart stirred, and he declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hulin he felt a sudden foreboding, declined the appointment, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 歸八日而父歿，未葬，火焚其廬。

translations.literal: Eight days after his return his father died; before the burial, fire burned down his cottage.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days after he returned, his father died. Before the funeral could be held, fire consumed the family dwelling.

sentences.zh: 溢搏顙天，火至柩所而滅。

translations.literal: Yi beat his forehead against heaven; when the fire reached the coffin, it went out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi beat his forehead and cried to Heaven, and when the flames reached the coffin they died away.

sentences.zh: 蘄、黃寇犯龍泉，溢從子存仁被執，溢挺身告賊曰：「吾兄止一子，寧我代。

translations.literal: Bandits from Qi and Huang raided Longquan; Yi's nephew Cunren was seized. Yi stepped forward and told the bandits: "My elder brother has only one son — let me take his place.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits from Qi and Huang invaded Longquan, Yi's nephew Cunren was captured. Zhang Yi stepped forward and said to the rebels, "My brother has only one son. Let me take his place instead.

sentences.zh: 」賊素聞其名，欲降之，縛於柱，溢不為屈。

translations.literal: " The bandits had long known his name and wished to win him over; they bound him to a pillar, but Yi did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long known his name and sought to win him over. They bound him to a pillar, but he refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 至夜紿守者脫歸，集裏民為義兵，擊破賊。

translations.literal: At night he deceived the guards and escaped; he gathered local people as a righteous militia and defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: By night he tricked his guards, escaped, rallied the local people into a militia, and routed the bandits.

sentences.zh: 俄府官以兵來，欲盡誅詿誤者。

translations.literal: Soon prefectural officials came with troops, intending to execute en masse those who had been misled.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward prefectural troops arrived and planned to execute everyone who had been implicated.

sentences.zh: 溢走說石抹宜孫曰：「貧民迫凍餒，誅之何為。

translations.literal: Yi went in haste to persuade Shimao Yisun, saying: "Poor people driven by cold and hunger — what use is it to execute them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi hurried to Shimao Yisun and argued, "These are poor people driven by hunger and cold. What is to be gained by killing them.

sentences.zh: 」宜孫然其言，檄止兵，留溢幕下。

translations.literal: " Yisun approved his words, issued a proclamation halting the troops, and kept Yi in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun agreed, issued orders to halt the troops, and retained Zhang Yi on his staff.

sentences.zh: 從平慶元、浦城盜。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the bandits of Qingyuan and Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the bandits in Qingyuan and Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 授龍泉主簿，不受歸。

translations.literal: He was appointed Recorder of Longquan, declined, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of Recorder of Longquan, but declined and returned home.

sentences.zh: 宜孫守台州，為賊所圍。

translations.literal: Yisun defended Taizhou and was besieged by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Yisun was defending Taizhou, he was besieged by bandits.

sentences.zh: 溢以鄉兵赴援，卻賊。

translations.literal: Yi came with local militia to relieve him and drove off the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi marched with local militia to relieve him and repelled the bandits.

sentences.zh: 已而賊陷龍泉，監縣寶忽丁遁去，溢與其師王毅帥壯士擊走賊。

translations.literal: Before long bandits captured Longquan; the supervising official Baohuding fled; Yi and his teacher Wang Yi led stalwart men and routed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bandits seized Longquan. The supervising official Baohuding fled, but Zhang Yi and his teacher Wang Yi led a force of stalwarts and drove the bandits off.

sentences.zh: 寶忽丁還，內慚，殺毅以反。

translations.literal: Baohuding returned, ashamed within, killed Yi and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Baohuding returned, ashamed of his flight, he killed Wang Yi and raised a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 溢時在宜孫幕府，聞之馳歸，偕胡深執戮首惡，因引兵平松陽、麗水諸寇。

translations.literal: Yi was then on Yisun's staff; hearing of it he raced home, together with Hu Shen seized and executed the chief culprit, then led troops to pacify the bandits of Songyang, Lishui, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi was then serving on Yisun's staff. When he heard the news he rushed home, and together with Hu Shen captured and executed the ringleader, then led troops to pacify the bandits in Songyang, Lishui, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 長槍軍攻婺，聞溢兵至，解去。

translations.literal: The Long-Spear Army attacked Wu; hearing that Yi's troops had arrived, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Long-Spear Army attacked Wu Prefecture, they withdrew on hearing that Zhang Yi's forces were approaching.

sentences.zh: 論功累授浙東都元帥府僉事。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Commissioner in the Eastern Zhejiang Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated merit he was repeatedly promoted, eventually to Vice Commissioner in the Eastern Zhejiang Marshal's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 溢曰：「吾所將皆鄉里子弟，肝腦塗地，而吾獨取功名，弗忍也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Those I command are all sons of our home district; their livers and brains are smeared on the ground — yet I alone would take merit and fame; I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi said, "The men I lead are all local youths who have shed their blood in battle. I cannot bear to take credit for myself alone.

sentences.zh: 」辭不受。

translations.literal: " He declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 以義兵屬其子存道，退隱匡山。

translations.literal: He entrusted the righteous militia to his son Cundao and retired to seclusion on Mount Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: He handed command of the militia to his son Cundao and withdrew to seclusion on Mount Kuang.

sentences.zh: 明兵克處州，避入閩。

translations.literal: When Ming forces took Chuzhou, he withdrew into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces captured Chuzhou, he fled into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 太祖聘之，與劉基、葉琛、宋濂同至應天。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor invited him, and together with Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Song Lian he came to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor invited him, and he traveled to Yingtian together with Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Song Lian.

sentences.zh: 太祖勞基等曰：「我為天下屈四先生，今天下紛紛，何時定乎？

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor consoled Ji and the others, saying: "I have humbled myself before the four masters for the sake of the realm — yet the realm is still in turmoil. When will it be settled?
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor welcomed Ji and the others and said, "I have bowed to the four masters for the sake of the empire, yet the empire remains in turmoil. When will it be settled?

sentences.zh: 」溢對曰：「天道無常，惟德是輔，惟不嗜殺人者能一之耳。

translations.literal: " Yi replied: "Heaven's way is without constancy; only virtue is its aid — only one who does not delight in killing men can unify it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi answered, "Heaven's way is inconstant; only virtue supports it. Only one who does not delight in killing can unify the realm.

sentences.zh: 」太祖偉其言，授僉營田司事。

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor admired his words and appointed him Vice Commissioner of the Land-Reclamation Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor was impressed by his words and appointed him Vice Commissioner in the Land-Reclamation Office.

sentences.zh: 巡行江東、兩淮田，分籍定稅，民甚便之。

translations.literal: He toured the fields of Jiangdong and the two Huai regions, divided households for registration and fixed taxes, and the people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the farmlands of Jiangdong and the two Huai regions, registered households, and fixed tax quotas, greatly easing the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 以病久在告，太祖知其念母也，厚賜遣歸省，而留其子存厚于京師。

translations.literal: Long ill and on leave, the Founding Emperor knew he missed his mother; he generously rewarded him and sent him home to visit, while detaining his son Cunhou in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had been ill on extended leave. The Founding Emperor knew he longed for his mother, gave him a generous gift, and sent him home to visit her, while keeping his son Cunhou in the capital.

sentences.zh: 浙東設提刑按察使，命溢為僉事。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Zhejiang Surveillance and Punishment Commission was established, he was ordered to serve as Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Zhejiang Surveillance Commission was established, Zhang Yi was appointed Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 胡深出師溫州，令溢守處州，饋餉供億，民不知勞。

translations.literal: Hu Shen marched to Wenzhou; Zhang Yi was ordered to hold Chuzhou, provision supplies in abundance, and the people did not feel the strain.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Shen marched on Wenzhou, Zhang Yi was left to hold Chuzhou. Supplies flowed in such abundance that the people barely felt the burden of war.

sentences.zh: 山賊來寇，敗走之。

translations.literal: Mountain bandits came to raid; he defeated them and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When mountain bandits raided, he defeated them and drove them away.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣按察僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Huguang Surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Huguang Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 時荊、襄初平，多廢地，議分兵屯田，且以控制北方。

translations.literal: At that time Jing and Xiang had only just been pacified; there was much abandoned land; it was proposed to divide troops for garrison farming and thereby control the north.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou and Xiangyang had only recently been pacified, and much land lay abandoned. He proposed dividing troops to farm garrison fields and thereby secure control of the north.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 會浙東按察使宋思顏、孔克仁等以職事被逮，詞連溢。

translations.literal: Just then Eastern Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner Song Siyan, Kong Keren, and others were arrested for official matters, and their testimony implicated Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Song Siyan and Kong Keren, commissioners of Eastern Zhejiang Surveillance, were arrested on official charges, and their testimony implicated Zhang Yi.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣太史令劉基諭之曰：「素知溢守法，毋疑也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sent Grand Astrologer Liu Ji to reassure him, saying: "I have long known Yi observes the law — do not doubt it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent Grand Astrologer Liu Ji to reassure him, saying, "I have long known that Yi is law-abiding. Do not doubt him.

sentences.zh: 」會胡深入閩陷沒，處州動搖，命溢為浙東按察副使往鎮之。

translations.literal: " Just then Hu Shen penetrated Fujian and was lost; Chuzhou was shaken; Zhang Yi was ordered to serve as Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Eastern Zhejiang and go to stabilize it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Hu Shen advanced into Fujian and was killed. With Chuzhou unsettled, Zhang Yi was appointed Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Eastern Zhejiang and sent to restore order.

sentences.zh: 溢以獲罪蒙宥，不應遷秩，辭副使，仍為僉事。

translations.literal: Yi, having been implicated yet pardoned, felt he did not deserve promotion; he declined the deputy post and remained Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been implicated but pardoned, Zhang Yi felt he did not deserve a promotion. He declined the deputy commissionership and remained Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既至，宣佈詔旨，誅首叛者，餘黨悉定。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he proclaimed the imperial edict, executed the chief rebels, and all remaining followers were settled.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he proclaimed the imperial edict, executed the ringleaders, and pacified the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 召舊部義兵分佈要害。

translations.literal: He summoned his old militia units and deployed them at strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled his former militia and stationed them at key positions.

sentences.zh: 賊寇慶元、龍泉，溢列木柵為屯，賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: When bandits raided Qingyuan and Longquan, Yi set up wooden palisades as encampments, and the bandits did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits threatened Qingyuan and Longquan, he erected wooden palisades as garrison posts, and the bandits did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 浦城戍卒乏食，李文忠欲運處州糧餉之。

translations.literal: Garrison troops at Pucheng lacked food; Li Wenzhong wished to transport grain from Chuzhou to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Pucheng was short of food. Li Wenzhong wanted to transport grain from Chuzhou to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 溢以舟車不通，而軍中所掠糧多，請入官均給之，食遂足。

translations.literal: Yi argued that boats and carts could not get through, but the army had captured much grain; he requested that it be turned over to the government and distributed equally, and provisions were thus sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi pointed out that transport by boat and cart was impossible, but that the army had seized ample grain. He proposed confiscating the looted grain for equal distribution, and the troops' food supply was restored.

sentences.zh: 溫州茗洋賊為患，溢命子存道捕斬之。

translations.literal: Bandits at Mingyang in Wenzhou were causing harm; Yi ordered his son Cundao to capture and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits at Mingyang in Wenzhou were causing trouble. Zhang Yi ordered his son Cundao to capture and execute them.

sentences.zh: 硃亮祖取溫州，軍中頗掠子女，溢悉籍還其家。

translations.literal: When Zhu Liangzu took Wenzhou, the army widely plundered women and children; Yi registered them all and returned them to their families.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Liangzu captured Wenzhou, his troops seized many women and children. Zhang Yi registered them all and returned them to their families.

sentences.zh: 吳平，詔存道守處，而召溢入朝。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, Cundao was ordered by edict to hold Chuzhou, while Yi was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, Cundao was ordered to remain and hold Chuzhou, while Zhang Yi was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖諭群臣曰：「溢雖儒臣，父子宣力一方，寇盜盡平，功不在諸將後。

translations.literal: Taizu instructed the ministers, saying, "Though Yi is a Confucian minister, father and son exerted strength in one region and bandits were all pacified; their merit is not behind the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told the ministers, "Though Zhang Yi was a Confucian civil official, he and his son exerted themselves in one region until the bandits were all pacified—their merit was no less than that of the leading generals.

sentences.zh: 」復問溢征閩諸將如何。

translations.literal: " He again asked Yi how the generals for the Fujian campaign were.
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked Yi what he thought of the generals assigned to the Fujian campaign.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「湯和由海道，胡美由江西，必勝。

translations.literal: He answered, "Tang He by the sea route and Hu Mei by Jiangxi will surely win.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Tang He by sea and Hu Mei through Jiangxi will surely prevail.

sentences.zh: 然閩中尤服李文忠威信。

translations.literal: Yet in Fujian they especially submit to Li Wenzhong's prestige and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people of Fujian especially respect Li Wenzhong's prestige and authority.

sentences.zh: 若令文忠從浦城取建寧，此萬全計也。

translations.literal: If Wenzhong is ordered from Pucheng to take Jianning, this is a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: If Wenzhong is sent from Pucheng to take Jianning, that would be a perfectly secure plan.

sentences.zh: 」太祖立詔文忠出師如溢策。

translations.literal: " Taizu at once ordered Wenzhong to march out according to Yi's plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu immediately ordered Wenzhong to take the field according to Yi's plan.

sentences.zh: 處州糧舊額一萬三千石，軍興加至十倍。

translations.literal: Chuzhou's grain quota had been thirteen thousand piculs; with the army's rise it was increased tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou's original grain quota was thirteen thousand piculs; with the outbreak of war it was raised tenfold.

sentences.zh: 溢言之丞相，奏復其舊。

translations.literal: Yi spoke of it to the chief councillor, who memorialized to restore the old amount.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported this to the chief councillor, who memorialized the throne to restore the original quota.

sentences.zh: 漸東造海舶，征巨材於處。

translations.literal: Eastern Zhejiang built seagoing ships and levied great timbers from Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhejiang was building seagoing vessels and requisitioning great timbers from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 溢曰：「處、婺之交，山岩峻險，縱有木，從何道出？

translations.literal: Yi said, "At the border of Chu and Wu, mountains and cliffs are steep and perilous; even if there is timber, by what road can it come out?
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "At the border of Chuzhou and Wuzhou the mountains are steep and perilous; even if timber exists there, by what road could it be brought out?

sentences.zh: 」白行省罷之。

translations.literal: " He informed the provincial administration and the levy was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " He reported this to the provincial administration, and the requisition was halted.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年與劉基並拜御史中丞兼贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was appointed Censor-in-Chief together with Liu Ji, concurrently Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongwu he was appointed Censor-in-Chief alongside Liu Ji, while also serving as Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣伺帝意，多嚴苛，溢獨持大體。

translations.literal: At the time court ministers watched the emperor's intent and were mostly harsh; Yi alone upheld the larger principle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many court officials watched the emperor's mood and prosecuted cases harshly; Yi alone upheld the larger principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 或以為言。

translations.literal: Some spoke against this.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials criticized him for it.

sentences.zh: 溢曰：「憲台百司儀表，當養人廉恥，豈恃搏擊為能哉！

translations.literal: Yi said, "The censorate is the model for all offices; it should nurture people's sense of shame—how can it rely on ferocious prosecution as its ability!
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "The censorate is the moral standard for all offices; it should cultivate people's sense of shame—how can it pride itself on ferocious prosecution alone!

sentences.zh: 」帝親祀社稷，會大風雨，還坐外朝，怒儀禮不合，致天變。

translations.literal: " The emperor personally sacrificed to the altars of soil and grain; a great wind and rain came; returning he sat in the outer court, angry that the ritual was not correct and had caused a heavenly change.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor personally sacrificed at the altars of soil and grain, a violent storm arose; on his return he sat in the outer court, furious that the ritual had been performed incorrectly and had provoked a heavenly portent.

sentences.zh: 溢委曲明其無罪，乃貰之。

translations.literal: Yi tactfully showed they were not guilty, and they were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tactfully demonstrated their innocence, and the emperor pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 文忠之征閩也，存道以所部鄉兵萬五千人從。

translations.literal: When Wenzhong campaigned in Fujian, Cundao followed with fifteen thousand local militia under his command.
translations.idiomatic: During Wenzhong's Fujian campaign, Cundao followed with fifteen thousand local militiamen under his command.

sentences.zh: 閩平，詔存道以所部從海道北征。

translations.literal: When Fujian was pacified, an edict ordered Cundao to lead his troops north by sea.
translations.idiomatic: After Fujian was pacified, an edict ordered Cundao to lead his troops north by sea.

sentences.zh: 溢持不可，曰：「鄉兵皆農民，許以事平歸農，今復調之，是不信也。

translations.literal: Yi held that it would not do and said, "The local militia are all farmers; they were promised that when affairs were settled they could return to farming—now to mobilize them again is to break faith.
translations.idiomatic: Yi objected, saying, "These militiamen are farmers who were promised they could return to their fields once peace was restored—to mobilize them again would break the government's word.

sentences.zh: 」帝不懌。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 既而奏曰：「兵已入閩者，俾還鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized, "Those troops already in Fujian should be sent back to their villages.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he memorialized, "The troops already in Fujian should be sent home to their villages.

sentences.zh: 昔嘗叛逆之民，宜籍為軍，使北上，一舉而恩威著矣。

translations.literal: The people who once rebelled should be registered as soldiers and sent north—in one move favor and awe will be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had formerly rebelled should be enrolled as soldiers and sent north—in a single stroke both mercy and authority would be made plain.

sentences.zh: 」帝喜曰：「孰謂儒者迂闊哉！

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and said, "Who says Confucians are impractical and broad!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted and said, "Who says Confucian scholars are impractical!

sentences.zh: 然非先生一行，無能辦者。

translations.literal: Yet without you, sir, going in person, none can carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet without you, sir, going in person, no one else could carry this out.

sentences.zh: 」溢行至處州，遭母喪，乞守制。

translations.literal: " Yi traveled to Chuzhou, encountered his mother's death, and asked to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi traveled to Chuzhou, where his mother died; he requested leave to observe the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 鄉兵既集，命存道由永嘉浮海而北，再上章乞終制。

translations.literal: Once the local militia were gathered, he ordered Cundao to sail north from Yongjia by sea, and again submitted a memorial asking to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Once the local militia were assembled, he ordered Cundao to sail north from Yongjia by sea and again submitted a memorial requesting permission to complete the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 溢悲戚過度，營葬親負土石，感疾卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: Yi's grief was excessive; in preparing the burial he personally carried earth and stone, took ill from emotion, and died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Yi grieved beyond measure; while preparing the burial he personally carried earth and stone, fell ill from overexertion and grief, and died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝痛悼，親撰文，即其家祭之。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply, personally composed a text, and sacrificed at his home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, composed a funeral text in his own hand, and conducted the sacrifice at Yi's home.

sentences.zh: 子 存道

translations.literal: Son: Cundao
translations.idiomatic: Son: Cundao

sentences.zh: 存道，溢長子。

translations.literal: Cundao was Yi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Cundao was Zhang Yi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 溢應太祖聘，存道帥義兵歸總管孫炎。

translations.literal: When Yi answered Taizu's invitation, Cundao led a loyalist force to join Chief Controller Sun Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi answered Taizu's invitation to serve, Cundao led a loyalist militia to join Chief Controller Sun Yan.

sentences.zh: 炎令守上游，屢卻陳友定兵。

translations.literal: Yan ordered him to guard the upper reaches and he repeatedly repelled Chen Youding's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yan ordered him to guard the upper reaches of the river, and he repeatedly repelled the forces of Chen Youding.

sentences.zh: 及以功授處州翼元帥副使，戍浦城。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made vice marshal of the Chuzhou wing and garrisoned Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was appointed vice marshal of the Chuzhou wing and garrisoned Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 總制胡深死，命代領其眾，為遊擊。

translations.literal: When Chief Controller Hu Shen died, he was ordered to take over his forces as a mobile striker.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Controller Hu Shen died, he was ordered to take command of his troops as a mobile strike force.

sentences.zh: 溢即處城坐鎮之。

translations.literal: Yi then sat in command at Chuzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi then took up command at Chuzhou city.

sentences.zh: 溢謂父子相統，於律不宜，奏罷存道官。

translations.literal: Yi said father and son commanding in succession was not proper by law and memorialized to dismiss Cundao from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi argued that father and son commanding in succession was improper under the law and memorialized to have Cundao removed from office.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 旋分兵征閩，而詔存道守處，復部鄉兵，從李文忠入閩。

translations.literal: Soon troops were divided to campaign in Fujian; an edict ordered Cundao to guard Chu, again organized the local militia, and followed Li Wenzhong into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward troops were divided for the Fujian campaign; Cundao was ordered to guard Chuzhou, reorganized the local militia, and followed Li Wenzhong into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 及還，浮海至京師。

translations.literal: When he returned, he sailed by sea to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he sailed by sea to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝褒諭之，命從馮勝北征。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and instructed him and ordered him to follow Feng Sheng on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded him and ordered him to join Feng Sheng's northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 積功授處州衛指揮副使。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was made vice commander of Chuzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was appointed vice commander of Chuzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年從徐達西征，留守興元，敗蜀將吳友仁，再守平陽，轉左衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he followed Xu Da on the western campaign, remained to guard Xingyuan, defeated the Shu general Wu Youren, again guarded Pingyang, and was transferred to vice commander of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he joined Xu Da's western campaign, remained behind to guard Xingyuan, defeated the Shu general Wu Youren, later guarded Pingyang, and was transferred to vice commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年從湯和出塞征陽和，遇敵於斷頭山，力戰死焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Tang He beyond the passes to campaign at Yanghe; he met the enemy at Mount Duantou, fought fiercely, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Tang He beyond the frontier to campaign at Yanghe; he encountered the enemy at Mount Duantou, fought fiercely, and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：太祖既下集慶，所至收攬豪雋，徵聘名賢，一時韜光韞德之士幡然就道。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: After Taizu took Jiqing, wherever he went he gathered bold and outstanding men and recruited famous worthies; for a time scholars who had hidden their light and stored their virtue turned about and took the road.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist writes: After Taizu captured Jiqing, wherever he advanced he gathered bold and talented men and recruited celebrated scholars; men who had long kept their gifts in obscurity came forward in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 若四先生者，尤為傑出。

translations.literal: Of the four masters, they were especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Among them the four masters were especially eminent.

sentences.zh: 基、濂學術醇深，文章古茂，同為一代宗工。

translations.literal: Ji and Lian had learning pure and deep, writings ancient and luxuriant, and together were patriarchs of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and Song Lian possessed learning of exceptional depth and writings of classical vigor; together they stood as masters of their age.

sentences.zh: 而基則運籌帷幄，濂則從容輔導，于開國之初，敷陳王道，忠誠恪慎，卓哉佐命臣也！

translations.literal: Ji then plotted within the tent, Lian calmly guided and instructed; at the founding of the state they expounded the kingly way—loyal, sincere, and reverently cautious—how eminent were these ministers who aided the mandate!
translations.idiomatic: Ji devised strategy within the command tent while Lian calmly guided and instructed; in the founding of the dynasty they expounded the kingly way with loyalty, sincerity, and scrupulous care—truly eminent ministers who aided the founding mandate!

sentences.zh: 至溢之宣力封疆，琛之致命遂志，宏才大節，建豎偉然，洵不負弓旌之德意矣。

translations.literal: As for Yi exerting strength on the frontier and Chen giving his life to fulfill his aim—great talent and great integrity, achievements towering and grand—they truly did not betray the virtue and intent of the bow-and-banner summons.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhang Yi exerting himself on the frontier and Ye Chen giving his life to fulfill his purpose—their great talent and integrity, their towering achievements— they truly did not betray the honor of the imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 基以儒者有用之學，輔翊治平，而好事者多以讖緯術數妄為傅會。

translations.literal: Ji, with the useful learning of a Confucian, assisted in governing peace, yet those who delight in such things mostly used omen texts, weft writings, and numerology to make reckless connections.
translations.idiomatic: Ji applied the practical learning of a Confucian scholar to assist in establishing peace, yet later enthusiasts often forced omen texts, cosmological lore, and numerology upon his story.

sentences.zh: 其語近誕，非深知基者，故不錄雲。

translations.literal: Their words verge on the absurd; they are not those who truly knew Ji, and so they are not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Such accounts verge on the absurd; they come from those who did not truly understand Ji, and are therefore not recorded here.
